Long-term tobacco smoke, air pollution, occupational dust or fumes

sections.heading: How airflow is limited
body: Airways carry air to elastic air sacs called alveoli. Normal air sacs fill on inhalation and deflate on exhalation. In COPD, damage to the lungs and airways restricts airflow and makes breathing difficult.

Chronic bronchitis involves an inflamed, swollen airway lining and excess mucus that narrow or clog the airways. Emphysema damages the walls between alveoli and reduces elasticity, which makes it harder to move air out. Most people with COPD have a varying mixture of emphysema and chronic bronchitis.

sections.heading: Symptoms, exposures and testing
body: Symptoms include breathlessness, especially with activity, a chronic cough with or without mucus, wheezing and fatigue. Long-term tobacco smoke, air pollution and occupational dust or fumes can contribute to COPD. Not everyone with COPD has smoked. Spirometry is a breathing test used to confirm COPD. Symptoms alone are not a diagnosis.

sections.heading: What care involves
body: COPD has no cure, but treatments can improve symptoms and the ability to stay active. Quitting smoking, avoiding lung irritants, appropriate vaccinations and pulmonary rehabilitation are parts of COPD care.

Bronchodilator inhalers relax the airway muscles and help keep the airways open. Correct inhaler technique matters, and care is individualized. Oxygen therapy is used when it is indicated for low blood oxygen, not routinely for everyone with COPD.

sections.heading: Flare-ups and emergencies
body: A sudden worsening is called a flare-up, or exacerbation. Suddenly worse symptoms are a reason to contact a healthcare provider right away. Severe trouble catching a breath or talking calls for emergency care.

2026-10-29-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) damages the macula, the part of the retina that supports sharp, straight-ahead central vision. Its exact cause is unknown, and treatment depends on the type and stage.
glance: The macula, part of the retina at the back of the eye
Comprehensive dilated eye examination and OCT imaging

sections.heading: The macula and central vision
body: The macula is part of the light-sensitive retina at the back of the eye. It supports sharp, straight-ahead central vision. AMD damages the macula with aging. Its exact cause is unknown. Age, family history and smoking increase the risk.

sections.heading: Dry and wet AMD
body: Dry AMD can feature yellow drusen beneath the retina and can progress to retinal atrophy. Wet AMD features abnormal vessels beneath the retina that may leak or bleed and distort the structure of the retina. These are different disease patterns, not a single sequence that every case follows.

sections.heading: Changes in vision
body: Early AMD may have no symptoms. Advanced disease can make straight lines look wavy and can blur or blank out central vision. Peripheral vision is generally preserved, which is different from complete blindness.
New wavy lines or changes in central vision require prompt assessment by an eye doctor. Straight lines that look wavy warrant seeing an eye doctor right away.

sections.heading: Evaluation and care
body: A comprehensive dilated eye examination and OCT imaging can help evaluate AMD. Treatment depends on the type and stage. Anti-VEGF eye injections treat wet AMD and can preserve vision. Selected patients with intermediate AMD may benefit from AREDS-type supplements recommended by a clinician. That is not a recommendation of supplements for everyone.
Quitting smoking, regular exercise and healthy eating may help lower the risk or slow AMD-related vision loss. Low-vision devices and rehabilitation can support daily activities.

2026-10-29-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease in which the immune system mistakenly attacks the lining of joints, causing inflammation, pain, stiffness and swelling. There is no current cure, but early diagnosis and appropriate treatment can ease symptoms and reduce joint damage.
glance: Small joints in the hands, wrists and feet
Often symmetrical on both sides, but presentations vary

sections.heading: An attack on the joint lining
body: RA is a chronic autoimmune disease. The immune system mistakenly attacks the lining of joints, causing inflammation, pain, stiffness and swelling. Over time, joint inflammation can damage cartilage and nearby bone. The infographic's schematic joint shows the lining, cartilage and bone. It does not show damage that is inevitable in every patient.
What triggers the immune attack is not fully understood. Smoking and family history are risk factors, not guarantees of disease.

sections.heading: Which joints, and how it feels
body: Small joints in the hands, wrists and feet are commonly affected. Symptoms often occur symmetrically, on both sides, but presentations vary. Common symptoms include tender, warm, swollen joints, prolonged stiffness after waking or rest, difficulty making a fist and fatigue.

sections.heading: Diagnosis and treatment
body: Early clinical evaluation matters. Diagnosis uses examination, blood tests and imaging, not symptoms alone. Early diagnosis and appropriate treatment can ease symptoms and reduce joint damage, though there is no current cure.

Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) are commonly prescribed, and a rheumatologist individualizes treatment and follow-up. Low-impact exercise and physiotherapy or occupational therapy can support strength, mobility and daily activities. Supplements do not replace RA medicines.

sections.heading: A sudden, severe joint
body: Sudden severe joint pain with swelling, difficulty moving the joint or fever needs urgent assessment for a possible joint infection. It is not something to assume is an RA flare, and fever may be absent. General education of this kind is distinct from a professional medical diagnosis and individualized treatment.

2026-10-30-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Tortoiseshell cats have mottled orange and non-orange fur and are nearly always female. The patches arise because one X chromosome is randomly inactivated in each cell early in development.
glance: Random inactivation of one X chromosome in each cell
Orange patches favor pheomelanin; black patches favor eumelanin

sections.heading: How the mosaic forms
body: Tortoiseshell cats have mottled orange and non-orange fur, and they are nearly always female. In a typical XX cat that carries both orange and non-orange variants, one X chromosome is randomly inactivated in each cell early in development.
The cells descended from those early cells retain different active X chromosomes. The result is a mosaic of pigment-cell areas, which appear as orange or black patches in the coat.

sections.heading: The orange variant
body: University accounts of two 2025 studies describe the deletion associated with orange fur. It is in a non-coding region at the ARHGAP36 locus, which is X-linked. Orange patches show increased ARHGAP36 activity in melanocytes, the pigment cells. Orange patches favor the pigment pheomelanin, and black patches favor eumelanin.

sections.heading: What the pattern does not show
body: The cell and chromosome artwork in the infographic is a simplified schematic of the mechanism, not a literal map of a cat's patches.
A coat-color pattern does not establish an individual cat's personality. These findings do not establish links between coat color and behavior.

2026-10-30-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Concentrated permethrin spot-on flea treatments intended for dogs can cause severe, potentially fatal poisoning in cats. A cat can be exposed when the product is applied to it, or through close contact with a recently treated dog.

sections.heading: A dog treatment that can poison cats
body: Concentrated permethrin spot-on flea treatments intended for dogs can cause severe, potentially fatal poisoning in cats. The guidance from the PDSA veterinary charity and the UK Veterinary Medicines Directorate is never to apply a dog-only flea treatment to a cat, not even part of a pipette.

Cats can also be exposed through close contact with a dog that was recently treated with permethrin, or by grooming it. The guidance is to keep cats away from treated dogs according to the product instructions.

sections.heading: Signs and urgent contact
body: Permethrin toxicity affects the cat's nervous system. It can cause drooling, wobbling, twitching, tremors and seizures. Suspected exposure warrants immediate contact with a veterinarian, even before signs develop. The guidance is to take the product packaging to the vet.

sections.heading: What the warning covers
body: The warning concerns concentrated spot-on products that are for dogs only. It is not a claim that every flea product, or every permethrin formulation, carries an identical risk. The guidance is to check which species a product is suitable for and to follow the product label.

2026-10-30-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The pinna is the cat's external ear flap. It can orient independently of the head, and its shape contributes to locating sounds, though the precise contribution of active pinna movements is not fully resolved.

Receives vibrations and passes signals toward the brain
The precise contribution of active pinna movements

sections.heading: The path of sound
body: The pinna is the external ear flap. Sound vibrations enter the ear canal and reach the eardrum. Small bones in the middle ear transmit them to the inner ear. The cochlea receives the vibrations and passes nervous-system signals toward the brain, which enables hearing.

sections.heading: Ears that move independently of the head
body: A cat's pinnae can orient independently of the position of its head. Pinna movements accompany orienting to sounds and to visual targets.

In the reported experimental conditions, a sound can evoke an early pinna movement that comes before the eye movement. That movement is asymmetric, larger in the ear on the side of the sound. The ear positions in the artwork are illustrative, not a universal fixed response.

sections.heading: How the ear helps locate sound
body: The pinna, head and torso weaken or strengthen different sound frequencies depending on the direction a sound comes from. This creates direction-dependent spectral cues for locating the sound.

The shape of the pinna contributes to sound localization. The precise functional contribution of active pinna movements is not fully resolved. The infographic does not claim perfect localization or a quantified improvement from moving the ears.

2026-10-30-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: A cat's slow blink is typically a run of half-blinks followed by longer eye narrowing or closure. Experiments suggest it may be a positive signal between cats and people, but it is read together with the rest of the face and body, not on its own.
glance: Half-blinks followed by prolonged eye narrowing or eye closure
Possibly positive cat-human communication, not proof of affection every time
Ears, tail, pupils and the rest of the body

sections.heading: What a slow blink looks like
body: A slow blink sequence typically involves half-blinks followed by prolonged eye narrowing or eye closure. It is a movement of the eyelids, and the infographic shows the eyelids moving, not the pupils changing size.

sections.heading: What the experiments found
body: In controlled experiments, cats half-blinked and narrowed their eyes more after their owners slow blinked than when there was no interaction. Cats were also more likely to approach an unfamiliar experimenter after slow blinking than after a neutral expression.

The results suggest that slow blinking may be a positive form of communication between cats and people. They do not make it a guaranteed translation of what a cat feels, or proof of affection in every instance.

sections.heading: Reading the whole cat
body: One eye signal does not stand alone. The face and the body posture supply the context. A relaxed cat can have upright ears and a tail that is not flicking and has no raised hairs.

Backward or flattened ears, a lashing tail and dilated pupils can come before petting-induced aggression. The veterinary guidance behind this part of the infographic is to stop petting when signs of aggression appear and to avoid handling a cat that has not invited it.

2026-10-30-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Scratching is normal behavior for a cat. It leaves visible marks and scent from the paws, helps remove the outer sheaths of the claws, and stretches the body.
glance: Visible marks, plus scent from glands on the paws
Helps remove superficial claw sheaths, not the entire claw
Stretches the body and maintains claw motion used in hunting and climbing
Cats differ in material and in vertical or horizontal orientation

sections.heading: A normal behavior, not revenge
body: Scratching is normal feline behavior. It is not evidence that a cat is seeking revenge. Cats differ in the materials they prefer to scratch, and in whether they prefer a vertical or a horizontal orientation.

sections.heading: Marks to see and to smell
body: Scratching leaves visible marks. It also deposits scent from glands on the paws. In this way it serves both visual communication and communication by smell. The scent itself is not visible.

sections.heading: Claw care and stretching
body: Scratching helps remove the superficial sheaths of the claws. The entire claw is not shed. Scratching also stretches the body and maintains the claw motion that a cat uses in hunting and climbing.

2026-10-31-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Tokophobia is an established term for a severe or phobic fear of childbirth, which is different from ordinary uncertainty about birth. The anxiety may occur even when someone wants a child.
glance: Severe or phobic fear of childbirth

Can follow a difficult or traumatic birth
Rapid heartbeat, muscle tension, disturbed sleep, panic symptoms
Midwife or obstetrician, perinatal mental-health referral, therapy such as CBT, collaborative birth plan

sections.heading: More than ordinary uncertainty
body: Tokophobia is an established term for severe or phobic fear of childbirth. It is not ordinary uncertainty about birth. Anxiety may occur even when someone wants a child, and symptoms and experiences vary.
Primary tokophobia can occur without prior experience of birth. Secondary tokophobia can follow a difficult or traumatic birth.

sections.heading: What the fear can involve
body: Anticipatory anxiety can increase during pregnancy. Thoughts about birth, negative accounts of birth and memories of a traumatic previous birth may be associated with fear. Fears may focus on harm to the parent or baby. Anxiety symptoms can include a rapid heartbeat, muscle tension, disturbed sleep and panic symptoms.
Avoidance can involve not talking or thinking about birth and avoiding antenatal education. Isolation and feeling unsupported can also occur.

sections.heading: Maternity and mental-health support
body: Guidance from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence is that people with tokophobia should be offered a discussion with a professional experienced in supporting this fear. Support can include speaking with a midwife or obstetrician, a perinatal mental-health referral, psychological therapy such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), and a collaborative birth plan that includes pain-relief and birth options.

Maternity teams discuss birth options and develop plans that account for both physical and mental health. Fear alone does not measure an individual's obstetric risk. Treatment is individualized to the symptoms and the anxiety condition, and education is not an individual diagnosis.

2026-10-31-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Chronophobia is an extreme fear of time or of time passing. It is a named fear described clinically within specific phobias, and the name does not imply a separate diagnostic code.
glance: Extreme fear of time or time passing
Named fear described clinically within specific phobias
Thinking about time passing, getting older or mortality
Palpitations, trembling, dizziness; symptoms vary between people
Psychotherapy; CBT is a treatment for phobias

sections.heading: What the name covers
body: Chronophobia means an extreme fear of time or time passing. It is a named fear described clinically within specific phobias. The name does not imply a separate diagnostic code.
Thinking about time passing, getting older or mortality can evoke intense discomfort or dread. Some people obsess over clocks or calendar days.

sections.heading: Symptoms, avoidance and isolation
body: Phobia symptoms can include palpitations, trembling and dizziness, and symptoms vary between people. People with specific phobias may avoid reminders of what they fear. Chronophobia can involve social isolation and interference with relationships.
Time cannot be stopped. A calendar or a clock is not itself an immediate danger, even when the alarm associated with it feels intense.

sections.heading: Therapy and managing symptoms
body: Psychotherapy can help with chronophobia, and cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a treatment for phobias. Talking to someone trusted and relaxation breathing may help manage symptoms. The NHS guidance is to seek professional help when symptoms affect daily life.

2026-10-31-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Somniphobia is an extreme fear of sleep. Even the thought of going to sleep may provoke extreme anxiety, and fear of sleep is not identical to insomnia.
glance: Thoughts of going to sleep can be enough to provoke fear

Talking therapies including CBT can help phobias

sections.heading: Fear of sleep and anticipation
body: Somniphobia means extreme fear of sleep. Even thinking of going to sleep may provoke extreme anxiety. Anticipatory anxiety means anxiety before the feared situation, and thoughts of going to sleep can be sufficient to provoke fear. Phobia symptoms can include palpitations, chest tightness and trembling. Responses vary between people.

sections.heading: What studies of PTSD found
body: In fear of sleep related to post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), anticipated nightmares and the inability to remain vigilant while asleep can contribute. This is not an explanation for every person. Hypervigilance means remaining on guard. In studied adults with PTSD and insomnia, fear of sleep is associated with greater hypervigilance.
Fear of sleep is not identical to insomnia. In the studied PTSD sample, it related to nightmares and hypervigilance, not to classic insomnia symptoms.
Avoiding sleep-related reminders may occur in trauma-related fear. Reliance on avoidance can make trauma symptoms worse and impede recovery.

sections.heading: Fear, danger and assessment
body: Fear can be disproportionate to a threat. The intensity of a fear response is not itself evidence of current danger. Real sleep symptoms warrant individual assessment.

sections.heading: Therapy and the limits of one trial
body: Talking therapies, including cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), can help phobias. A health professional is relevant when symptoms affect daily life. In a trial of adults with both PTSD and insomnia, cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) reduced fear of sleep. That finding is specific to the group studied. It is not a universal promise.

2026-10-31-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Thanatophobia is an established term for fear of death. Awareness of mortality is common, and not all worry about death is illness. Distress and disruption of daily life are what warrant assessment.
glance: An established term; not presented as a separate diagnosis
Death-related conversations and news; thoughts of one's own death
Palpitations, dizziness, trembling; symptoms differ between people
CBT, addressing unhelpful beliefs and avoidance

sections.heading: A common awareness, an established term
body: Thanatophobia is an established term for fear of death. Death anxiety is studied across multiple mental health conditions, and the term is not presented here as a separate diagnosis.
Awareness of mortality is common. Distress and disruption of daily life warrant assessment. It is not assumed that all death-related worry is illness.

sections.heading: Reminders and the body's alarm
body: Death-related conversations and news can act as reminders that provoke death anxiety, and thoughts of one's own death can be feared. Phobic anxiety may include palpitations, dizziness and trembling. Symptoms differ between people.
Perceived threat can exceed the current situation. A reminder or a frightening thought is not itself evidence of imminent death.

sections.heading: Avoidance and short-term relief
body: Avoiding death-related reminders can be an unhelpful coping behavior that maintains death anxiety. Short-term relief is not the same thing as lasting recovery.

sections.heading: Support planned with a clinician
body: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) can reduce death anxiety by addressing unhelpful beliefs and avoidance. Individualized professional assessment is relevant when fear disrupts life.

The sources say any exposure work should be planned collaboratively with a trained clinician, using safe, gradual steps and not forced confrontation, and that normal medical care should be maintained.

2026-10-31-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Megalophobia is an established name for an intense fear of large objects. It is discussed clinically as a specific phobia, not as a separately named DSM diagnosis.
glance: Discussed clinically as a specific phobia
Large buildings, statues and vehicles, or thinking about large objects
Rapid heartbeat, shortness of breath, dizziness, urge to escape; experiences vary
Cognitive behavioral therapy and gradual exposure therapy tailored to the person

sections.heading: The name and the triggers
body: Megalophobia is an established name for intense fear of large objects. It is discussed clinically as a specific phobia, not as a separately named DSM diagnosis. Large buildings, statues and vehicles can trigger the fear. Thinking about large objects can also provoke anticipatory anxiety.

sections.heading: Symptoms and proportion
body: Symptoms can include a rapid heartbeat, shortness of breath, dizziness and an urge to escape. Experiences vary. Phobic fear is out of proportion to the actual danger of the object or situation.

sections.heading: Avoidance and daily life
body: Avoidance can provide short-term relief. It also prevents a person from learning that fear can be managed and that feared outcomes often do not happen. Anxiety symptoms can interfere with daily routines and activities, and professional assessment is relevant when fear limits daily life.

sections.heading: How gradual exposure is described
body: Cognitive behavioral therapy helps change responses to anxiety. Gradual exposure therapy is tailored to the person by a therapist or psychologist. Exposure treatment can begin with talking about large objects, then move to pictures, then to being near an object. The pace is gradual and individualized.

2026-10-31-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Nosophobia, also called disease phobia, is a persistent fear of developing a specific serious disease. It overlaps with health anxiety and illness anxiety disorder, and which diagnosis applies is for a clinician to assess, not something a label can settle.
glance: Persistent fear of developing a specific serious disease
Health anxiety and illness anxiety disorder
Bodily sensations and disease-related health information
Body checking, searching for health information, seeking reassurance, avoiding reminders of serious illness
Cognitive behavioral therapy, for health anxiety and related illness anxiety

sections.heading: What the term means
body: Nosophobia is an established term in the medical literature, also called disease phobia. It refers to a persistent fear of contracting or having a dangerous disease, and the fear is often focused on a specific serious illness. In plain English, it is a persistent fear of developing a specific serious disease.

The term is descriptive. Health anxiety and illness anxiety disorder are related to it and overlap with it, but the name does not settle a diagnosis. A clinician has to assess which diagnosis is appropriate. It cannot be inferred from a label.

sections.heading: How a sensation becomes an alarm
body: Bodily sensations and health information about disease can become cues for catastrophic interpretation. People may misinterpret a sensation as a sign of serious illness and overestimate the threat.
Anxiety itself can cause a racing heartbeat, and that heartbeat may then be misinterpreted as illness. A strong feeling of alarm does not by itself establish that a disease is present.

sections.heading: Checking, relief and persistence
body: The cognitive behavioral model of health anxiety links a chain of steps: a bodily cue, a catastrophic interpretation about illness, anxiety, and then checking, reassurance-seeking or avoidance. Those bring short-term relief. The fear persists because the feared beliefs remain untested. This is the model for health anxiety, a related problem. It is a model, not every person's pathway.
People may repeatedly check their bodies, search for health information, seek reassurance, or avoid reminders of serious illness and medical settings.

sections.heading: Therapy and clinical care
body: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is evidence-based help for health anxiety and related illness anxiety. It addresses catastrophic beliefs, vigilance toward the body, excessive checking, reassurance seeking and avoidance.

The sources point to seeing a clinician when health worries impair daily life, and they describe assessment and appropriate care as important. Reducing excessive checking belongs inside a care plan. It does not mean abandoning appropriate medical care. Educational material, this infographic included, does not diagnose illness.

2026-11-03-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Milky seas are rare expanses of ocean that give off a steady whitish glow at night. Luminous bacteria are implicated, but the conditions that produce the glow remain uncertain.

sections.heading: A steady glow, not a flash
body: Milky seas are rare expanses of steady, whitish marine bioluminescence that are visible at night. The glow may persist for days to weeks and drift with surface currents. Its steadiness sets it apart from the bioluminescence of dinoflagellates, which is mechanically stimulated and typically flashes briefly.

sections.heading: The bacterial explanation
body: Luminous bacteria are implicated in milky seas. A milky sea sampled in 1985 contained luminous bacteria associated with microalgae. At high bacterial population density, chemical quorum sensing can trigger bacterial luminescence. The precise ecological relationships of the bacteria, and the conditions that produce milky seas, remain uncertain.

sections.heading: Detecting the glow from orbit
body: The VIIRS day-night band can detect the faint glow from orbit under favorable conditions. Moonlight and clouds can complicate detection.

sections.heading: The larva and its prey
body: The larvae of Chrysoperla rufilabris are predators. They pass through three instars, and they have legs and large, curved, paired mouthparts. They impale aphids and suck out the body contents.

sections.heading: From stalked egg to winged adult
body: Eggs are laid singly on silken stalks on foliage. A mature larva spins a round silken cocoon, and the pupa develops before the adult emerges.

Adults are pale green, with golden eyes, long antennae and transparent wings. Adult size is roughly 12 to 20 mm. While the larvae are predators, Chrysoperla adults feed on nectar, pollen and honeydew.

sections.heading: Where it is found
body: Chrysoperla rufilabris is a green lacewing found in North America. The humid habitats where it is found include irrigated crops and greenhouses.

sections.heading: The generalized internal view
body: The internal anatomy in the infographic is a generalized insect body plan, not one specific to this lacewing. Spiracles admit air into branching tracheae, the alimentary canal carries food, and the ventral nerve cord runs along the body.

2026-11-03-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Sinking particles carry organic carbon from the sunlit surface of the ocean toward the deep. The carbon starts with phytoplankton, the particles feed deep-sea life, and some carbon reaches deep waters and sediments.

sections.heading: Carbon captured at the surface
body: In sunlit water, phytoplankton use photosynthesis to convert carbon dioxide into organic carbon. Phytoplankton can aggregate into sinking particles known as marine snow. Zooplankton eat phytoplankton and produce fecal pellets that contain carbon, and these pellets also sink.

sections.heading: What the sinking particles deliver
body: Sinking particles transport organic carbon from surface waters toward the deep ocean. Marine snow provides food to deep-sea animals and to organisms on the seafloor.

Some of the carbon reaches deep waters and sediments, where it can remain stored for long periods. The infographic follows phytoplankton, marine snow and zooplankton pellets as they move organic carbon into the deep ocean.

sections.heading: A gift during courtship
body: During courtship, the male Panorpa communis presents a collected insect to a female as a nuptial gift. Scorpionflies may also offer secreted saliva.

sections.heading: A tail that is not a sting
body: The curved, bulbous tip of the male's abdomen is his genitalia, used in mating. It is not a sting. The female's abdomen tapers. Panorpa scorpionflies have four patterned wings, a yellowish-brown body and a long beak that bears chewing mouthparts.
Scorpionflies are small insects. The body length of 3/8 inch applies to Panorpa generally and is not a precise measurement for this species.

sections.heading: A scavenger of woodland edges
body: Panorpa communis is a scorpionfly in the order Mecoptera. In the UK it is found at woodland edges and in hedgerows, on nettles and brambles. Adults scavenge dead invertebrates and may take insects from spider webs.
As described for Panorpa, the eggs are laid in a moist environment. The larvae scavenge, and they pupate in soil.

sections.heading: The generalized internal view

sections.heading: The hellgrammite
body: The eastern dobsonfly, Corydalus cornutus, is a megalopteran in the family Corydalidae, found in eastern North America. Its aquatic larva is called a hellgrammite. The larva is flattened, dark and segmented, with three pairs of legs on the thorax and sharp mandibles. It is approximately 2 to 3 inches long.
Aquatic larvae live beneath rocks or logs in streams and prey on aquatic animals. Hooked appendages at the end of the abdomen help the hellgrammite resist the stream current.

sections.heading: Gills along the abdomen
body: The larval abdomen has eight pairs of filaments along its sides, with cottony gill tufts at their bases. In insects, gills allow dissolved oxygen to diffuse into the body, and they are usually outgrowths of the tracheal system. The internal breathing diagram in the infographic is generalized.

sections.heading: From stream to land to air
body: Development is by complete metamorphosis. It proceeds from egg to aquatic larva, then to a pupa on land, then to a winged adult. Larval development takes several years.

sections.heading: The winged adult
body: Adults have long antennae, three pairs of legs and two pairs of prominently veined wings, which are held over the body at rest. They can exceed 3.5 inches in length. The mandibles of males are long and sickle-shaped. Those of females are much shorter.

sections.heading: Where it lives and what it eats

sections.heading: Life around the host anemone

sections.heading: How to recognize it
body: The Banggai cardinalfish is a silver fish with black bars, white spots and elongated fins. Adults reach a length of up to 8 cm.

sections.heading: Where it lives and what it eats
body: The species is native to the Banggai archipelago, where it lives on shallow coral reefs and in seagrass. It is a carnivore that eats small crustaceans.

body: The male broods the eggs in his mouth. Pairs may be aggressive toward other fish of their own species.

sections.heading: In an aquarium
body: The care notes draw on husbandry guidelines from an association of animal keepers. In captivity the fish is given varied meaty foods. The guidelines describe a mixed reef aquarium with small, non-aggressive fish and hiding places, and they prefer captive-bred fish.

Sharp, at the base of the tail; can cause painful injury

sections.heading: How to recognize it
body: The Pacific blue tang, Paracanthurus hepatus, has a blue, oval body with dark markings and a yellow tail. Adults average 25 to 31 cm in length.

sections.heading: Life on the reef
body: This fish lives on tropical coral reefs of the Indo-Pacific. It is often found near branching coral and in places with currents. The Pacific blue tang eats algae and zooplankton. It shelters in coral and may live in groups.

sections.heading: The tail spine and aquariums
body: The Pacific blue tang has a sharp spine at the base of its tail. The spine can cause a painful injury. In aquariums, surgeonfish such as this one can clash.

2026-11-05-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an immune-mediated disorder of the brain and spinal cord. Immune attacks damage the myelin coating around nerve fibers, and may damage the fibers themselves, which disrupts communication.
glance: Central nervous system: brain and spinal cord
Myelin, the protective coating around nerve fibers
Can occur in the brain and spinal cord and can be seen with MRI

sections.heading: Myelin and nerve signals
body: Multiple sclerosis is an immune-mediated disorder affecting the central nervous system, which is the brain and spinal cord. Myelin is the protective coating around nerve fibers. In MS, immune attacks damage the myelin around axons and may damage the axons themselves, disrupting communication. Demyelinated lesions can occur in the brain and spinal cord and can be seen with MRI.

The exact cause is unclear. Genetic susceptibility and environmental factors contribute. Smoking and prior Epstein-Barr virus infection are associated with increased risk, not with certainty of disease.

sections.heading: Symptoms and course
body: Symptoms vary by person and by where the lesions are. Fatigue, visual problems, numbness or tingling, muscle weakness or stiffness, and balance problems can occur.
Some people have relapses and remissions. Others experience progressive worsening. The course varies and cannot be predicted from a single illustration.

sections.heading: Diagnosis and treatment
body: No single test diagnoses MS. A neurologist combines history and examination with MRI, and sometimes spinal fluid or other tests, while excluding other causes.

There is no current cure. Disease-modifying therapies can reduce relapses and slow progression for appropriate patients, and treatment depends on the type of disease and individual needs. Corticosteroids may speed recovery from a relapse but do not change the long-term course. Physiotherapy, tailored exercise, fatigue management and medicines for symptoms can help.

sections.heading: Sudden symptoms and stroke
body: Sudden arm weakness or numbness, sudden vision loss or sudden balance problems can signal a stroke and require emergency medical help. They are not to be assumed to be MS. MS-like symptoms can have other causes and need to be checked by a clinician. General education is not diagnosis.

2026-11-05-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Acute pancreatitis is sudden inflammation of the pancreas, in which digestive enzymes can damage pancreatic tissue. It causes sudden, severe abdominal pain that needs urgent medical evaluation, and it is treated in the hospital.
glance: Behind the stomach, near the duodenum

Monitoring, IV fluids and pain relief
Most people recover; severe illness can be life-threatening

sections.heading: The pancreas and its enzymes
body: The pancreas lies behind the stomach, near the duodenum. It makes insulin, and it makes digestive enzymes that normally help digest food in the intestine. Acute pancreatitis is sudden inflammation of the pancreas. In it, digestive enzymes can damage pancreatic tissue.

sections.heading: What causes it
body: Gallstones and heavy alcohol use are common causes. Gallstones can block the opening of the pancreas. Some medicines and other conditions can also cause acute pancreatitis.

sections.heading: Symptoms and urgent warning signs
body: Symptoms include sudden, persistent, severe upper abdominal pain that may spread to the back, along with nausea, vomiting and fever. Sudden severe persistent abdominal pain needs urgent medical evaluation. Severe pain spreading to the back, a fast heartbeat or difficulty breathing warrants emergency care.

sections.heading: Evaluation and hospital treatment
body: Evaluation uses history, examination, blood tests and sometimes imaging such as CT. Hospital treatment includes monitoring, IV fluids and pain relief. Treating the cause may include gallstone surgery or support to stop drinking alcohol. Antibiotics are for infection, not a routine cure.

Most people recover, but severe illness may cause tissue death or infection and can be life-threatening. Reducing or avoiding alcohol, stopping smoking and following a clinician's dietary advice may help prevent recurrence.

2026-11-05-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: In a urinary tract infection, bacteria, usually from the bowel, can enter through the urethra and multiply in the bladder. An untreated bladder infection can develop into a kidney infection.
glance: Two kidneys, two ureters, a bladder and a urethra
Through the urethra to the bladder

Antibiotics, often used for bacterial bladder infection

sections.heading: The urinary tract and how infection starts
body: The urinary tract includes two kidneys, two ureters, a bladder and a urethra. The kidneys produce urine. The ureters carry it to the bladder, the bladder stores it, and the urethra carries it outside the body.

Bacteria, usually from the bowel, can enter through the urethra and multiply in the bladder. An untreated bladder infection can develop into a kidney infection. Catheters, impaired bladder emptying, pregnancy and menopause can increase the risk.

sections.heading: Symptoms and assessment
body: Symptoms are burning urination, urgency, frequency, lower abdominal discomfort and sometimes blood in the urine. Smell or dark urine alone does not establish a urinary tract infection. Clinical assessment uses symptoms and history and may include urine testing. Urine testing is not always needed.

sections.heading: Treatment and urinary health
body: Antibiotics are often used for a bacterial bladder infection, and the guidance is to take prescribed treatment as directed. Rest and appropriate fluids may help symptoms. Cranberry products do not treat an established infection.
Not holding urine, taking time to empty the bladder and drinking appropriate fluids may help urinary health. Where a clinician has set fluid limits, those limits apply.

sections.heading: Signs that need urgent help
body: Fever or chills, back pain below the ribs, blood in the urine, pregnancy or rapid worsening warrant urgent medical advice. New confusion, marked drowsiness or difficulty speaking warrant emergency help.

2026-11-05-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Achilles tendinopathy is a load-related problem of the tendon that connects the calf muscles to the heel bone. It causes pain, stiffness and swelling, and it is not the same as a complete rupture.
glance: Achilles tendon, connecting the calf muscles to the heel bone (calcaneus)
Noninsertional (middle of the tendon) and insertional (heel attachment)
Repetitive stress, a sudden increase in exercise, tight calf muscles
Morning stiffness, pain worsened by activity, swelling

sections.heading: The tendon and where it is affected
body: The Achilles tendon connects the calf muscles to the heel bone, the calcaneus. It is used during walking, running, jumping and standing on tiptoes. Repetitive stress, a sudden increase in exercise and tight calf muscles can contribute to Achilles tendon problems.

Noninsertional disease affects the middle of the tendon. Insertional disease affects its attachment at the heel. Affected tendon fibers can develop tiny tears, degeneration, swelling and thickening. This is not the same as a complete rupture.

sections.heading: Symptoms and assessment
body: Symptoms include morning stiffness, pain along the tendon or heel that is worsened by activity, and swelling. Assessment starts with history and examination. Imaging may be selected, and MRI is not always needed for diagnosis.

sections.heading: Management and recovery
body: Reducing the activity that aggravates the tendon, supportive footwear and physical therapy that includes supervised strengthening can help. Treatment must be tailored to the individual. Recovery can take months, and persistent symptoms call for assessment by a clinician.

sections.heading: Signs of a possible rupture
body: Sudden severe pain or a pop at the back of the calf or heel may signal a rupture and requires urgent medical assessment.

2026-11-05-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Vitiligo is a chronic condition in which skin loses pigment because working melanocytes, the cells that make melanin, are lost. It is not an infection and is not contagious.

sections.heading: Loss of pigment cells
body: Vitiligo is a chronic condition. Pigment is lost because working melanocytes, the cells that make melanin, are lost. In the common form, non-segmental vitiligo, the immune system attacks melanocytes.
Vitiligo is not an infection and is not contagious. A family history and other autoimmune conditions can be associated with it.

sections.heading: How it appears
body: In non-segmental vitiligo, white patches often appear on both sides, including the hands and face. Hair in affected areas can turn white. The extent of vitiligo and how it progresses vary.

sections.heading: How it is diagnosed
body: Diagnosis uses an examination of the skin. A Wood lamp can help distinguish pigment loss, and selected patients may need thyroid testing. New pale patches call for assessment, not self-diagnosis.

sections.heading: Sun protection and treatment
body: Affected skin is vulnerable to sunburn, so high-SPF sunscreen and sun protection are important. Treatment can include topical medicines supervised by a clinician. Camouflage is optional. Response varies, and no cure is guaranteed. Support for the emotional impact can help.

2026-11-06-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The nutritional adequacy statement on a cat food label says whether the food is complete and balanced and which life stage it is intended for. It is a different thing from the ingredient list.

sections.heading: What the statement says
body: The nutritional adequacy statement identifies whether a food is complete and balanced, and the life stage it is intended for. A complete and balanced food is intended as a sole diet. Treats, snacks and supplements typically are not.

sections.heading: How a food qualifies
body: A complete and balanced claim has to be backed in one of two ways. The food must meet an AAFCO nutrient profile, or it must pass a feeding trial that uses AAFCO procedures.

sections.heading: Not the ingredient list
body: The ingredient list is a separate part of the label. Its ingredients are ordered by decreasing weight, and it is not the nutritional adequacy statement.

sections.heading: What cats need from food
body: Cats need protein, fats, vitamins, minerals, fatty acids and amino acids. More supplementation is not automatically better. The Cornell guidance is to choose a food that is appropriate to the cat, with veterinary guidance. The infographic is general education, not a diet plan for an individual cat.

2026-11-06-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: White spotting in domestic cats leaves patches of coat without pigment, from tiny marks to extensive white areas. It is associated with an insertion in the KIT gene and is distinct from Dominant White.

sections.heading: How much white
body: White spotting ranges from tiny white patches to extensive white areas. The cats on the infographic are examples of that range. They are illustrations, not a scale of genotypes.

sections.heading: Why the patches have no color
body: The white areas lack skin melanocytes, the cells that produce pigment. This is different from a failure to make pigment. In white spotting, the pigment-producing cells are missing from the white areas of skin.

sections.heading: Two different insertions at KIT
body: White spotting in cats is associated with an insertion of a full-length feline endogenous retrovirus in intron 1 of KIT.
Dominant White is associated with a distinct, shorter insertion at KIT, a viral LTR. White spotting and Dominant White are distinct phenotypes.

2026-11-06-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) must never be given to cats. A cat's liver is deficient at breaking the drug down, which makes it potentially fatal.

sections.heading: Why it is dangerous to cats
body: Acetaminophen, sold as Tylenol, must never be given to cats. A cat's liver is deficient at breaking the drug down, and that makes it potentially fatal.
Acetaminophen can damage red blood cells and reduce their ability to carry oxygen. It can also damage the liver.

sections.heading: Signs that can appear
body: The American College of Veterinary Pharmacists lists signs that can include weakness, rapid or difficult breathing, blue-purple mucous membranes, vomiting, and swelling of the face or paws.

sections.heading: Where it turns up, and what happens next
body: Acetaminophen may be present in multi-symptom cold and allergy products. The same source says to keep medicines out of the reach of animals.

Suspected ingestion requires immediate contact with a veterinarian or with animal poison control, and accidental ingestion is to be reported immediately. The ASPCA Animal Poison Control Center hotline is (888) 426-4435.

2026-11-06-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The muscles around a cat's shoulder blade, the scapula, lie in layers. The rhomboideus sits beneath the trapezius, the serratus ventralis is a deep fan-shaped muscle on the side of the trunk, and the latissimus dorsi covers part of the chest wall.

sections.heading: Trapezius and rhomboideus
body: The trapezius extends from the midline of the back to the spine of the scapula, the shoulder blade. The rhomboideus lies deep to the trapezius, that is, beneath it. It attaches to the dorsal border of the scapula.

sections.heading: Serratus ventralis and latissimus dorsi
body: The serratus ventralis is a deep, fan-shaped muscle on the side of the trunk. It has a neck part and a thoracic part. The latissimus dorsi covers part of the chest wall. It lies superficial to deeper shoulder structures, which means nearer the surface.

sections.heading: Chest muscles and a small clavicle
body: The pectoral muscles occupy the underside of the chest. Both superficial and deep layers are present. The cat also has a small clavicle, or collarbone, which lies in the brachiocephalicus at the shoulder.

2026-11-06-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Flehmen is a pause that follows a cat's investigation of scent material. It helps chemical cues carried in fluid reach the vomeronasal organ, a paired sense organ near the roof of the mouth.
glance: Flehmen, which follows investigation of scent material
The paired vomeronasal organ, near the roof of the mouth
Nasopalatine canals, to the oral and nasal cavities
The detailed central processing in cats

sections.heading: What flehmen does
body: Flehmen follows a cat's investigation of scent material. It aids the access of fluid-borne chemical cues to the vomeronasal organ.
The vomeronasal organ is paired and lies near the roof of the mouth. Nasopalatine canals connect it with both the oral cavity and the nasal cavity.

sections.heading: Inside the organ
body: In its middle portion, the vomeronasal duct has sensory receptor epithelium on its medial side and respiratory epithelium on its lateral side. Glands, vessels, nerves and supporting cartilage surround the duct.

sections.heading: Main and accessory systems
body: Sensory neurons of the vomeronasal organ send their axons to the accessory olfactory bulb. The main olfactory epithelium detects volatile chemicals that are inhaled. The accessory system is associated with fluid-borne chemical cues. The functions of the two are not completely exclusive.

sections.heading: What is and is not known
body: Chemical communication takes part in social recognition and reproduction. How the cat's central nervous system processes these cues in detail remains incompletely understood.

2026-11-06-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: A defensive cat may crouch low with its head tucked and its tail curved around or tucked under its body. The crouch is one of a cluster of signals, and a pose alone does not establish its cause.

sections.heading: What the posture looks like
body: A defensive cat may crouch low with its head tucked and its tail curved around or tucked under its body. Ears flattened sideways or backward, and wide eyes with dilated pupils, can accompany defensive postures.
Hissing and raised fur may accompany fear-related defensive behavior. Not every sign must be present in a cat that is behaving defensively.

sections.heading: Reading the signs together
body: The guidance is to read the body posture, face, ears and tail together, and to consider the events that came before. A pose alone does not establish its cause.

sections.heading: Space, and when a veterinarian is involved
body: Fear-related aggression can escalate if a cat cannot escape. The ASPCA guidance is not to touch, restrain or punish a cat that is displaying defensive aggression, and to give it space until it is calm.
Pain or medical problems may contribute to aggression. According to the sources, new or persistent changes warrant veterinary assessment.

2026-11-07-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Autophobia, also called monophobia, is an extreme fear of being alone. It is not the same as loneliness, and the fear can arise without any immediate threat.
glance: When alone, when anticipating being alone, or when worrying that people will leave

Palpitations, trembling, dizziness and severe worry, varying between people
CBT, with gradual exposure planned individually

sections.heading: An extreme fear of being alone
body: Autophobia is an extreme fear of being alone. Monophobia is another name for it. Cleveland Clinic describes autophobia as a specific phobic disorder, though the descriptive name is not itself a separate diagnostic code.
The fear can occur when a person is alone, when they anticipate being alone, or when they worry that people will leave.

sections.heading: How it differs from loneliness
body: Autophobia differs from loneliness. Loneliness concerns the quantity or quality of a person's connections. Autophobia involves anxiety about being alone.
A phobic fear can occur without an immediate threat, and being alone is not in itself proof of danger. That does not cancel out genuine hazards.

sections.heading: Body alarm and avoidance
body: Phobia symptoms can include palpitations, trembling, dizziness and severe worry, and they vary between people. Thinking about a feared situation can be enough to trigger anxiety or panic. Avoidance can come to organize daily life and to limit it.

sections.heading: Treatment and clinical support
body: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is an evidence-based talking treatment used for phobias. Gradual exposure is used in treatment. It is planned for the individual, with professional help where needed.
The NHS sources point to clinical support if fear interferes with daily life. Educational illustrations such as this one are not a diagnosis.

2026-11-07-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Algophobia is an extreme fear of physical pain. Fear and avoidance can reduce activity and may worsen disability and pain, though the pattern varies between people, and fear of pain does not mean the pain is imaginary.
glance: Thinking about pain, anticipated movement, reminders of painful experiences
Intensely monitoring for pain or threat

CBT, and an individualized, clinician-guided gradual return to suitable activities

sections.heading: A clinical term for fear of pain
body: Algophobia is an established clinical term for an extreme fear of physical pain. The term is descriptive. It is not a claim that the fear has a separate diagnostic code.

sections.heading: Triggers, thoughts and body alarm
body: Thinking about pain, an anticipated movement, and reminders of painful experiences can trigger anxiety and avoidance. The body's alarm can include palpitations, sweating, trembling and shortness of breath.
In this context, catastrophizing means that a person imagines the worst outcome, and hypervigilance means intensely monitoring for pain or threat.

sections.heading: The fear-avoidance pattern
body: Fear-avoidance can reduce activity and participation, and it may worsen disability and pain. The pattern varies between people.
Actual pain and fear of pain both merit assessment. A sense of threat is not a direct measure of tissue injury, and fear does not mean that pain is imaginary.

sections.heading: Help planned with the healthcare team
body: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) can help change pain-related thoughts. An individualized, clinician-guided gradual return to suitable activities can help with fear of pain. The sources add that treatment should address the actual pain too.
Professional help is the step the sources point to when fear interferes with daily life. Treatment is planned with the healthcare team, not by forcing painful exposure.

2026-11-07-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Atychiphobia is an intense fear of failure. The worry can start before an event such as an exam or a job interview, and it is not the same thing as perfectionism.
glance: Potential failure in exams or job interviews
Severe worry, palpitations, trembling and feeling sick, though not in everyone

sections.heading: Fear of failure, not perfectionism
body: Atychiphobia means an intense fear of failure. It is an established descriptive name for a phobia, not a separate diagnostic code. Atychiphobia and perfectionism are not the same. Fear of failure differs from striving to be flawless.

sections.heading: What sets it off
body: Potential failure in an exam or a job interview can trigger the fear. Worry about failing can arise before the event itself.
Phobia symptoms can include severe worry, palpitations, trembling and feeling sick. These are possible symptoms, and they are not universal.

sections.heading: Felt threat and avoidance
body: A phobia can feel genuinely threatening, and intense fear need not match the situation. A possible unsuccessful outcome is not the same as immediate physical danger.
People may avoid situations in which failure is possible. That avoidance can impair how a person performs at work or at school.

sections.heading: Talking therapy
body: Talking therapy such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) can help with phobias. The NHS guidance is to seek professional help when symptoms affect a person's life.

2026-11-07-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Phonophobia is a persistent fear of sound. Everyday sounds such as traffic, closing doors and loud speech can set it off even at non-damaging levels, and the term is not interchangeable with hyperacusis.
glance: Traffic, closing doors and loud speech, even at non-damaging levels
Can include palpitations, sweating and trembling
Can mean sound intolerance, not a phobic disorder
CBT, which may include professionally guided graded exposure

sections.heading: A word with more than one use
body: Phonophobia is an established clinical term for a persistent fear of sound. That is the sense used here: fear of sound, not a separately named diagnostic category.

In migraine literature the same word can mean sound intolerance and not a phobic disorder. Phonophobia and hyperacusis are also not interchangeable. Hearing-related and emotional components can overlap, and they require clinical assessment.

sections.heading: Sounds, anticipation and arousal
body: Environmental sounds such as traffic, closing doors and loud speech can trigger fear, even at non-damaging levels. Autonomic arousal can include palpitations, sweating and trembling.
Anticipation of feared sounds and learned reactions can accompany avoidance of situations that involve sound. That avoidance may restrict social participation and daily life.

sections.heading: Fear does not measure acoustic danger
body: Fear is not a measurement of acoustic danger, and sounds that do no damage can trigger it. Genuinely hazardous noise is a separate matter. It should not be used for exposure.

sections.heading: Treatment and hearing assessment
body: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is an evidence-based talking therapy used for phobias. Professionally guided graded exposure may be part of treatment. It follows an individualized, safe plan and is not forced exposure to loud sound.

The sources point to a clinician if fear affects daily life. Painful sound or concerns about hearing merit a hearing assessment. General education is not diagnosis. The journal source is a case report, so it does not show how common phonophobia is or how treatment turns out for other people.

2026-11-07-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Ombrophobia is an extreme fear of rain. Light drizzle, heavy rain or simply anticipating rainfall may set it off, and avoiding the outdoors when rain is possible can restrict daily life.

sections.heading: Where the name fits
body: Ombrophobia is an extreme fear of rain. The name is an established descriptive one, and the fear falls within specific phobia, which is an anxiety disorder.

sections.heading: Drizzle, downpours and forecasts
body: Triggers may include light drizzle, heavy rain or the anticipation of rainfall. Phobias can involve severe worry, palpitations, trembling and dizziness, and symptoms vary between people.
A person may recognize that the fear is unreasonable and still find it difficult to control. The consequences a person fears are not evidence of actual danger.

sections.heading: Staying in when rain is possible
body: Worrying about forecasts and refusing to go outdoors can disrupt everyday activities. Avoiding outings, or skipping activities when rain is possible, can restrict daily life.

sections.heading: Talking therapies
body: Talking therapies, including cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), can help with phobias. The NHS guidance is to seek professional help when symptoms affect a person's life.

2026-11-07-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Thermophobia is a descriptive term for a persistent fear of heat. Heat can also cause actual illness, so physical symptoms must not simply be assumed to be anxiety.
glance: Severe worry, palpitations, trembling, dizziness and fear of losing control

sections.heading: How the term is used
body: Thermophobia is an established descriptive term for fear of heat. Heat-related situations and hot objects can trigger anxiety. A published case report uses the name for a fear involving hot food.
The word names a fear and is not a claim of a separate diagnostic category. The meaning, persistent fear of heat, was also checked in the medically edited RxList dictionary.

sections.heading: Symptoms and avoidance
body: Phobias can involve severe worry, palpitations, trembling, dizziness and a fear of losing control. Symptoms differ between people.

Avoiding feared circumstances can bring short-term relief. The cited case reports avoidance, and symptoms that subsided spontaneously. That is what happened in a single reported case. It is not a universal mechanism for all patients.

sections.heading: Real heat risks
body: Heat can cause actual illness. The CDC guidance behind the infographic is to stay cool and hydrated, use shade and cooling, and take local heat-risk advice seriously.
Symptoms of overheating can include heavy sweating, dizziness, headache, weakness and nausea. Physical symptoms must not simply be assumed to be anxiety.

sections.heading: Help for the phobia
body: Phobias can interfere with daily life. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a talking therapy used to treat phobias. The guidance in the sources is to seek professional help if symptoms affect a person's life.

2026-11-10-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Internal waves are vertical disturbances within the density layers of the ocean. Tidal flow over a submarine ridge can generate them.

sections.heading: How they form
body: Internal waves are vertical disturbances within the density layers of the ocean. Tidal flow over a submarine ridge can generate them. The infographic follows that case: tidal water flows across an underwater ridge, and internal waves then propagate along the density layers.

sections.heading: What the waves do
body: Once generated, internal waves propagate through the ocean. They can also contribute to the mixing of water masses, which is one of the effects the infographic covers.

sections.heading: Seeing them from above
body: Internal waves are disturbances within the water, but they can produce patterns at the surface. Those surface patterns are detectable in satellite imagery.

2026-11-11-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The royal gramma, also called the fairy basslet, is a small purple and yellow reef fish of the western Atlantic and Caribbean. It stays close to ledges, caves and overhangs and feeds mainly on planktonic crustaceans.
glance: Reefs of the western Atlantic and Caribbean
Close to reef ledges, walls, caves and overhangs

sections.heading: How to recognize it
body: The royal gramma has an elongate body that is flattened from side to side, a large eye and a short snout. The front of the body is purple and the rear is yellow. A black spot marks the front of the dorsal fin, yellow lines radiate from the eye, and the pelvic fins have elongated rays. The fish reaches approximately 8 cm in total length, about 3 inches.
The accepted species is Gramma loreto Poey, 1868. Royal gramma and fairy basslet are both common names, and the U.S. Geological Survey reports no scientific synonyms.

sections.heading: Life along the ledges
body: This is a reef fish of the western Atlantic and Caribbean. It lives close to reef ledges, walls, caves and overhangs, and it may swim upside down with its belly facing the roof.

It feeds primarily on planktonic crustaceans. It may also remove external parasites from other fishes, but it is not an obligate cleaner. Groups on the reef are territorial and have dominance hierarchies based on size. Larger fish occupy the prime feeding positions.

sections.heading: Nests and egg care
body: Males build nests in crevices and care for the eggs, which are demersal, meaning they rest on the bottom. Once the sexes have differentiated they stay separate. The species does not routinely change from female to male.

sections.heading: What this means for an aquarium
body: The aquarium points on the infographic are planning implications drawn from the biology, not tested minimum standards. Shelter and feeding access should be consistent with the ledge habitat and the plankton diet. Because the fish is territorial, groups seen in the wild do not imply that a group will be compatible in an aquarium. Small fish and invertebrates can be prey, so reef-safe is not an absolute guarantee.

The species has been bred in captivity. Aquarium fish should never be released. The occurrence of this species outside its native range has been associated with possible aquarium release as well as natural expansion.

2026-11-11-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The firefish, or red firegoby, is a small coral-reef fish that hovers just above the bottom, facing into the current to eat zooplankton. It retreats into a burrow when disturbed.
