sections.heading: How to recognize it
body: The firefish, also called the red firegoby, has an elongate white first dorsal fin, a yellow snout and a white head. The body is white and grades to bright orange-red toward the rear. The fish raises and waves its long first dorsal fin, and aquarium and university sources describe this as fin signaling.
Clearwater Marine Aquarium gives a maximum size of up to 3 inches, about 7.6 cm. That is an approximate reported upper size, not a precise measurement that applies to every adult.

sections.heading: Where it lives
body: The firefish is a coral-reef fish of the tropical Indo-Pacific and Central Pacific, with a range that includes East Africa to Pitcairn. It lives on outer reef slopes at 6 to 61 m.

sections.heading: Feeding in the current, hiding in burrows
body: The firefish often hovers within 0.5 m above the bottom, facing into the current to eat zooplankton, especially copepods and other crustacean larvae.
It uses holes in the bottom as burrows and retreats when disturbed. Adults live alone or in pairs, while several juveniles may share one hole.

sections.heading: What this means for an aquarium
body: The aquarium recommendations on the infographic are inferred from the biology described by its sources. They are to supply refuges the fish can reach and suitably small planktonic foods, and to avoid large predators. Clearwater Marine Aquarium lists triggerfish, lionfish and large angelfish as threats.

Pairing in the wild is not a guarantee that any group will be compatible, and plankton feeding alone does not establish that the fish is safe in every reef tank. The infographic gives no numeric tank minimum and no blanket guarantee of safety with corals or invertebrates.

2026-11-11-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The mandarinfish is a small bottom-dwelling fish of western Pacific coral reefs and shallow lagoons. It feeds by day on tiny invertebrates, and feeding it in an aquarium can be difficult.
glance: Tropical coral reefs and shallow lagoons, on the bottom among coral and rubble
6 to 9 cm in one source; a maximum of 6 cm in another
Small crustaceans and other tiny invertebrates, including copepods and worms
Scaleless, with a thick mucus coating

sections.heading: How to recognize it
body: The mandarinfish has a broad, flattened head, a small mouth and wavy blue-green and orange markings. The male has an elongated first dorsal spine, and the fanlike pelvic fins are used at the bottom. The skin has no scales and carries a thick coating of mucus. The secretion may deter predators.
Adults are small. The Aquarium of the Pacific reports 6 to 9 cm (2.4 to 3.5 inches), while the Animal Diversity Web reports a maximum of 6 cm, so there is no single agreed maximum.

sections.heading: Where it lives and how it feeds
body: The mandarinfish lives on tropical coral reefs and in shallow lagoons of the western Pacific. It is a bottom dweller, found among coral and rubble.

It feeds by day on the bottom, taking small crustaceans and other tiny invertebrates, including copepods and worms. The food comes from the substrate and live rock. The fish is usually shy and mostly passive.

sections.heading: Why aquarium care is difficult
body: Feeding a mandarinfish in an aquarium can be difficult, and many individuals do not accept prepared food. The implication for husbandry is to verify that a fish keeps taking suitably tiny food over time. The presence of live rock alone does not show that. Small body size does not mean easy care. Males can fight in an aquarium, so the advice is to avoid pairing males.

Reef compatibility depends on diet. Tiny invertebrates are prey, so the fish cannot be promised safe in every reef tank. That caution is an inference from the documented diet, not a blanket safety classification.

2026-11-11-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The longnose hawkfish is a slender reef fish with a very long, thin snout and a red cross-hatch pattern. It perches on gorgonians or black coral and feeds on zooplankton and small crustaceans.
glance: Indo-Pacific and eastern Pacific, including the Red Sea
5 to 100 m in total, generally on deeper reef

sections.heading: How to recognize it
body: The longnose hawkfish has a whitish body with horizontal and vertical red bands that form a cross-hatch grid. The body is slender and flattened from side to side, and the snout is very long and thin. The fish grows to 13 cm, about 5.1 inches.
Tufts of cirri sit at the tips of the dorsal spines. The lower rays of the pectoral fins are stout and elongated, and the fish uses them for perching.

sections.heading: Where it lives and what it eats
body: Its marine range covers the Indo-Pacific and the eastern Pacific, including the Red Sea. It perches on gorgonians or black coral. Its reef habitat is generally deeper, with a reported total depth range of 5 to 100 m and some shallow exceptions.
The Oregon Coast Aquarium describes its food as zooplankton and small crustaceans. The pointed mouth helps it capture small prey.

sections.heading: What this means for an aquarium
body: The aquarium points on the infographic are labeled as inferences, not tested universal compatibility. They are to provide stable structure for perching and suitable small meaty foods. Small crustacean tankmates may be prey, so the fish cannot be promised safe in every reef tank. Its association with this habitat does not prove that all corals or all companions are safe. No numeric tank minimum is given.

2026-11-12-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Hypertension is persistently high pressure of blood against the walls of the arteries. It usually has no symptoms, yet over time it can damage the heart, brain and kidneys.
glance: Persistently high pressure of blood against artery walls
Measured between beats, while the heart fills
Above 180 systolic and/or above 120 diastolic, with symptoms

sections.heading: Pressure in the arteries
body: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Hypertension means persistently high pressure of blood against the artery walls. Systolic pressure is the pressure while the heart is pumping. Diastolic pressure is measured between beats, while the heart fills.

sections.heading: Why it goes unnoticed
body: High blood pressure usually has no symptoms. Measurements help establish the diagnosis. They are often repeated over visits and taken with a validated home monitor.
Over time, high blood pressure can damage the heart, brain and kidneys. It increases the risk of heart attack, heart failure, stroke and kidney disease.

sections.heading: Risk factors and care
body: Risk factors include family history, increasing age, excess sodium, inactivity and excess alcohol. Multiple factors can contribute. Care can include a heart-healthy DASH eating pattern, limiting sodium and alcohol, physical activity and medicines prescribed to the individual.

sections.heading: When a high reading is an emergency
body: Pressure higher than 180 systolic and/or higher than 120 diastolic, together with chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness, a change in vision or difficulty speaking, is an emergency. The CDC guidance is to call 911. For pressure that high without symptoms, the guidance is to contact a healthcare professional.

2026-11-12-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Benign prostatic enlargement, or BPH, is noncancerous enlargement of the prostate that becomes more common with age. The enlarged prostate can squeeze the urethra and impede the flow of urine.
glance: Below the bladder, around the urethra at the bladder neck
Uncertain; age-related hormonal changes may contribute
Prostate size does not reliably predict symptom severity

sections.heading: How outflow narrows
body: BPH is noncancerous enlargement of the prostate. It becomes more common with age. Its cause is uncertain, and age-related hormonal changes may contribute.

The prostate lies below the bladder and surrounds the urethra at the bladder neck. Enlargement can squeeze the urethra and impede urine flow. The bladder works harder against the narrowed outflow and may eventually fail to empty fully, leaving residual urine.

sections.heading: Urinary symptoms
body: Symptoms can include difficulty starting, a weak or interrupted stream, incomplete emptying, frequency, urgency and nighttime urination. Prostate size does not reliably predict how severe the symptoms are. Other urinary disorders can cause similar symptoms and require evaluation.

sections.heading: Evaluation and management
body: Evaluation includes history, examination and urine tests. Selected patients may need PSA testing, urine-flow testing or a bladder ultrasound.

Mild symptoms may be monitored. Reducing caffeine and alcohol, and shifting fluids away from bedtime while maintaining daytime hydration, may help. Alpha blockers, selected by a clinician, relax muscles in the prostate and bladder neck. Clinician-selected 5-alpha reductase inhibitors can help shrink the prostate. Procedures may relieve obstruction when symptoms are severe or medicines fail. Treatment has benefits and risks and is individualized.

sections.heading: Urgent warning signs
body: Being unable to urinate, blood in the urine, or painful, urgent urination with fever and chills or severe lower abdominal pain are reasons to seek urgent medical care.

2026-11-12-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Scoliosis is a sideways curve of the spine, shaped like a C or an S, in which the vertebrae also twist or rotate. Most scoliosis in adolescents is idiopathic, meaning its exact cause is unknown.
glance: Sideways C- or S-shaped curve, with twisted or rotated vertebrae
Thoracic and lumbar regions may be involved
Idiopathic (exact cause unknown); can run in families

sections.heading: A curve and a twist
body: Scoliosis can form a sideways curve shaped like a C or an S. The vertebrae also twist or rotate. The thoracic and lumbar regions of the spine may be involved. Asymmetry of the shoulders, ribs, waist and hips can be signs.

sections.heading: What is known about the cause
body: Most adolescent scoliosis is idiopathic, which means its exact cause is unknown. It can run in families. Poor posture and heavy backpacks do not cause idiopathic scoliosis. Small curves are often painless and go unnoticed. Growth spurts can worsen a curve.

sections.heading: Examination and treatment
body: Clinical examination includes the forward bend test, which reveals rib asymmetry. X-rays locate and measure the curve. Treatment depends on the size and location of the curve and on how much growth remains. Many mild curves are observed. Bracing for selected growing children helps prevent a curve from progressing. It does not straighten an existing curve. Surgery may be considered for severe or progressing curves. Most children and teens can lead normal, active lives with appropriate follow-up.

sections.heading: Pain that needs prompt evaluation
body: Severe back pain, or pain with weakness or numbness in a limb, warrants prompt medical evaluation for other causes.

2026-11-12-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Hyperthyroidism means the thyroid produces too much thyroid hormone, which speeds many body functions. Symptoms vary, and diagnosis requires clinical assessment and thyroid blood tests, not symptoms alone.
glance: Small, butterfly-shaped, in the front of the neck
The thyroid produces too much thyroid hormone

sections.heading: An overactive thyroid
body: The thyroid is a small butterfly-shaped gland in the front of the neck. Its hormones regulate energy use and affect nearly every organ. Hyperthyroidism means the thyroid produces too much thyroid hormone, speeding many body functions. Graves disease is an autoimmune cause that stimulates excess hormone production. Overactive nodules are another cause.

sections.heading: Symptoms and testing
body: Possible symptoms include heat intolerance, sweating, hand tremor, weight loss despite increased appetite, and a rapid or irregular heartbeat. Symptoms vary.
Diagnosis requires clinical assessment and thyroid blood tests, not symptoms alone. TSH, T4 and T3 tests help evaluate thyroid function.

sections.heading: Treatment options
body: Treatment is individualized by cause, severity and circumstances. Antithyroid drugs reduce hormone production. Beta blockers ease symptoms but do not stop hormone production. Radioiodine or surgery are options for selected patients. Radioiodine is not used during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

sections.heading: Complications and thyroid storm
body: Untreated hyperthyroidism can cause heart rhythm problems and bone thinning. Thyroid storm is a rare, life-threatening emergency. A high fever, a pounding rapid heart and confusion in someone with hyperthyroidism warrant calling emergency services.

2026-11-12-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Tennis elbow, or lateral epicondylitis, is a load-related problem where a wrist extensor tendon attaches to the outer bony prominence of the elbow. Playing tennis is not required to get it.
glance: Lateral epicondyle, the outer bony prominence of the humerus

sections.heading: The outer elbow attachment
body: The elbow contains the humerus, radius and ulna. The lateral epicondyle is the outer bony prominence of the humerus. Tendons connect muscle to bone. The ECRB wrist extensor tendon attaches at the lateral epicondyle and is commonly involved in tennis elbow.
Repeated vigorous use of the forearm can damage the tendon attachment, with degeneration and sometimes microscopic tears. This is not necessarily a complete tendon rupture.

sections.heading: What brings it on
body: Gripping, repetitive wrist extension or twisting in work, hobbies and racquet sports can contribute. Tennis is not required, and sometimes no repetitive injury is identified.

sections.heading: Symptoms and assessment
body: Symptoms include pain and tenderness on the outside of the elbow, a weak grip, and pain that is worsened by gripping or wrist movement. Symptoms often develop gradually.
Assessment uses the history of symptoms and an examination. Tests or imaging may be used to exclude other causes and are not necessarily required for everyone.

sections.heading: How it is managed
body: Care includes reducing the activities that worsen symptoms. Physiotherapy with stretching and strengthening of the wrist and forearm can help, and a forearm strap or brace may ease symptoms. Surgery is considered for persistent symptoms after prolonged nonsurgical treatment. It is not an automatic first step. Pain that persists despite self-care is a reason to seek medical review.

sections.heading: Arm pain that is urgent
body: A hot, swollen elbow with fever or chills, or severe pain with difficulty moving, warrants urgent assessment. An injury with deformity or snapping also needs urgent assessment. Sudden arm pain with chest pressure, heaviness or squeezing requires emergency help, and is not to be assumed to be tennis elbow.

2026-11-12-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: In chronic sinusitis, the lining of the sinuses is inflamed and swollen, which interferes with mucus draining into the nose and throat. It is driven more by inflammation than by infection.
glance: Air spaces behind the cheekbones and forehead, connected to the inside of the nose
Saline nasal irrigation and nasal steroid sprays

sections.heading: Sinuses and their drainage
body: Sinuses are air spaces behind the cheekbones and forehead that connect to the inside of the nose. A swollen sinus lining interferes with the drainage of mucus into the nose and throat.
Chronic sinusitis is driven more by inflammation than by infection, and antibiotics are not always helpful. Allergies, nasal polyps and asthma can accompany sinusitis and make it worse.

sections.heading: Symptoms and evaluation
body: Symptoms can include facial pressure or tenderness, a blocked nose, nasal discharge and a reduced sense of smell. Prolonged or repeated symptoms warrant clinical evaluation. CT may be needed for prolonged symptoms or suspected complications, but not routinely for uncomplicated sinusitis.

sections.heading: Treatment
body: Saline nasal irrigation and nasal steroid sprays are the main treatments for the symptoms of chronic sinusitis. For irrigation at home, the NHS describes boiling the water and then cooling it before use.
Endoscopic surgery may help selected chronic cases that are not controlled by medicines. It works by widening the natural drainage pathways of the sinuses.

sections.heading: When urgent help is needed
body: The reasons given for seeking urgent medical help are being very unwell, symptoms that worsen or are not helped by painkillers, and weakened immunity.

2026-11-13-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Many cats are lactose intolerant. They do not have enough lactase in the intestine to digest lactose, the sugar in milk, so dairy can cause digestive problems.
glance: Vomiting, diarrhea and stomach pain; not every cat becomes ill

sections.heading: Why milk can cause trouble
body: Lactose is the sugar in milk. Lactase in the intestine is needed to digest it, and many cats lack enough lactase. Many cats are lactose intolerant, and dairy can cause gastrointestinal problems.
The PDSA veterinary team notes that drinking milk that contains lactose can cause vomiting, diarrhea and stomach pain. Not every cat becomes ill.

sections.heading: Milk, water and cat milk
body: Adult cats do not need milk when they are fed an appropriate complete, balanced diet. Cats should always have clean, fresh water available. Reduced-lactose or lactose-free cat milk still adds calories, and it is often not a complete meal.

2026-11-13-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Agouti is the banding of pigment within a single cat hair. ASIP interacts with MC1R to switch between two pigments as the hair grows, and this banding is distinct from the tabby pattern across the coat.
glance: Agouti, pigment bands within a single hair
ASIP interacting with MC1R during hair growth

sections.heading: How the bands form
body: ASIP interacts with MC1R to switch the pigment deposited in a hair between eumelanin and phaeomelanin. The switching happens during hair growth, and it creates bands within the hair.

sections.heading: Bands are not stripes
body: Banding within a hair is distinct from the tabby pattern, which is laid out across the coat. In a brown tabby, the hairs between the dark stripes are banded. The hairs in the stripes remain dark.

sections.heading: How it is inherited
body: The genotypes A/A and A/a support agouti banding. Two copies of the recessive a produce non-agouti hairs, which are solid.
The overall appearance of a coat depends on other genes as well. Orange cats can retain tabby markings regardless of their agouti genotype.

2026-11-13-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Swallowed string can act as a linear foreign body in a cat and cause intestinal obstruction. Once the string anchors, the intestine gathers into pleats along it, and the string can erode through the intestinal wall.
glance: Swallowed string acting as a linear foreign body
Around the base of the tongue, or at the pylorus (stomach outlet)
The intestine gathers into pleats along the string (plication)
Vomiting, appetite loss and abdominal pain; presentation varies

sections.heading: How a string becomes a hazard
body: Swallowed string can act as a linear foreign body in cats and cause intestinal obstruction. The string can anchor around the base of the tongue or at the pylorus, the outlet of the stomach.

Peristaltic movement then gathers the intestine into pleats along the anchored string. This pleating is called plication. The string can erode through the intestinal wall, which causes leakage and life-threatening peritonitis.

sections.heading: Signs and assessment
body: Vomiting, loss of appetite and abdominal pain are possible signs, and the presentation varies. Suspected ingestion of a foreign object needs immediate veterinary care. Veterinarians use the history, an examination and imaging to assess it.

sections.heading: How it is removed
body: Some foreign bodies in the upper digestive tract can be removed endoscopically. Linear foreign bodies often require surgery, and severely damaged bowel may require resection, the surgical removal of that part.

2026-11-13-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: A domestic cat's claw is protruded by muscle pull and retracted by elastic ligaments. The deep digital flexor muscle pulls through its tendon to protrude the claw, and the elastic ligaments retract it passively.
glance: The deep digital flexor muscle contracts and pulls its tendon
The lateral ligament is especially important; a pair of dorsal elastic ligaments
Protects claws from wear when not in use

sections.heading: The bones of the digit
body: The distal phalanx and the middle phalanx meet at the distal interphalangeal joint. In digits 2 to 5 of the domestic cat's forepaw, the distal phalanx overlaps the middle phalanx when the claw is retracted.

sections.heading: Tendon pull
body: To protrude the claw, the deep digital flexor muscle contracts. Its tendon carries the pull to the flexor process of the distal phalanx. This protrudes the claw and stretches the elastic ligaments.

sections.heading: Elastic return
body: Elastic ligaments retract the claw passively. The lateral ligament is especially important, and there is also a pair of dorsal elastic ligaments. Retraction protects the claws from wear when they are not in use.

2026-11-13-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: A cat's vestibular apparatus lies deep in the inner ear. Its semicircular canals respond to rotation speeding up or slowing down, and its utricle and saccule respond to straight-line motion and gravity.
glance: Vestibular apparatus, deep in the inner ear beside the cochlea
Three, in different planes; respond to rotational acceleration or deceleration
Respond to linear acceleration or deceleration and gravity
Vestibular portion of cranial nerve VIII

sections.heading: Where the vestibular apparatus sits
body: The vestibular apparatus lies deep in the inner ear, beside the cochlea. It communicates with centers in the brainstem. The vestibular portion of cranial nerve VIII carries information from the receptors toward the brainstem.

sections.heading: Canals that sense rotation
body: Three semicircular canals occupy different planes. Each has an ampulla that contains a crista with sensory hair cells. The receptors of the semicircular canals respond to rotational acceleration or deceleration, which is rotation speeding up or slowing down.

sections.heading: Sensing straight-line motion and gravity
body: The utricle and the saccule contain sensory maculae. These respond to linear acceleration or deceleration, which is motion in a straight line speeding up or slowing down, and to gravity.

sections.heading: What the information is used for
body: Vestibular information helps stabilize posture and the eyes during head movement. It does this through the vestibulospinal and vestibulo-ocular reflexes. The infographic shows the normal anatomy and how it works. It is not a chart of disease.

2026-11-14-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Iatrophobia is a fear of doctors. It can involve extreme fear of doctors or medical tests, beyond the actual danger, and it may lead people to avoid medical attention they need.
glance: Severe worry, palpitations, dizziness, nausea and trembling
Avoiding necessary medical attention, even when sick

sections.heading: Fear of doctors and medical tests
body: Iatrophobia means fear of doctors. It can involve an extreme fear of doctors or of medical tests, beyond the actual danger. Cleveland Clinic describes it as a specific phobic disorder.

sections.heading: Symptoms and possible origins
body: Phobia symptoms can include severe worry, palpitations, dizziness, nausea and trembling. Phobias may relate to frightening experiences, but the causes are not always clear.

sections.heading: When fear keeps people from care
body: Fear may lead people to avoid necessary medical attention, even when they are sick. The infographic explains the fear through an imagined close clinical encounter, and it does not portray clinicians as dangerous.

sections.heading: Treatment and ways of coping
body: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a talking therapy used to treat phobias. The NHS guidance is to seek professional help when symptoms affect a person's life.
The same guidance says that talking to a trusted person and relaxation breathing can help manage phobia symptoms.

2026-11-14-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Chionophobia is an intense fear of snow. Seeing snow or wintry weather, or even thinking about a light snowfall, can trigger severe anxiety that exceeds the actual danger.
glance: Natural-environment specific phobia, as Cleveland Clinic describes it
Seeing snow or wintry weather, or thinking about light snowfall
CBT; gradual exposure or desensitization for simple phobias

sections.heading: A natural-environment phobia
body: Chionophobia means an intense fear of snow. Cleveland Clinic describes it as a specific phobia of the natural-environment type. It is not a separate named diagnostic code.

sections.heading: Snow, anticipation and body alarm
body: Seeing snow or wintry weather can trigger severe anxiety, and so can even the thought of a light snowfall. Phobias can involve anticipatory anxiety, and they can produce palpitations, trembling and dizziness.

sections.heading: Alarm compared with danger
body: Phobic alarm can exceed the actual danger. A light snowfall can provoke severe anxiety even without immediate danger. That does not imply that all winter conditions are safe. The infographic shows an imagined photographic scene, not a clinical case.

sections.heading: Staying indoors through winter
body: Phobias can bring an overwhelming urge to avoid the feared situation, which limits daily activities. Avoiding snow can mean staying indoors during winter, with disruption of work and relationships.

sections.heading: Treatment options
body: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a treatment option. Gradual exposure or desensitization is used for simple phobias. A specialist can help, and no single program works for everyone. The sources point to professional help when fear disrupts daily life.

2026-11-14-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Selenophobia is an intense fear of the moon or moonlight. A person may avoid looking at the moon or going out at night, though the sense of threat does not mean the moon presents a real one.
glance: Intense fear of the moon or moonlight
Looking at the moon and going out at night
Palpitations, trembling, dizziness and chest tightness, differing between people

sections.heading: Fear of the moon or moonlight
body: Selenophobia is an intense fear of the moon or moonlight. It is described as a specific phobia. It is not a separate named diagnostic category.

sections.heading: Anxiety, symptoms and avoidance
body: Thinking about the moon can provoke anxiety. Phobia symptoms can include palpitations, trembling, dizziness and chest tightness, and they differ between people.
People may avoid looking at the moon or going out at night. The threat is a perceived one. It does not mean that the moon or moonlight presents a real threat.

sections.heading: Treatment
body: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a treatment for phobias. The NHS guidance is to see a health professional if symptoms affect everyday life.

2026-11-14-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Amaxophobia is a fear of driving or riding in a vehicle. Even thinking about a journey may bring on anxiety, and feeling endangered is not proof that a crash is imminent.
glance: Fear of driving or riding in a vehicle
May include a crash or injury
CBT; gradual exposure may be used with professional support

sections.heading: Fear as driver or passenger
body: Amaxophobia means fear of driving or riding in a vehicle. It is a specific phobic disorder, not a separate stand-alone diagnostic category.

sections.heading: Anxiety ahead of a journey
body: Thinking about a vehicle journey may trigger anticipatory anxiety. The outcomes a person fears may include a crash or an injury. Phobia symptoms can include palpitations, sweating and trembling, which are bodily anxiety responses.

sections.heading: The sense of danger
body: Phobias involve an exaggerated or unrealistic sense of danger. Feeling endangered is not proof that a crash is imminent.

sections.heading: Avoidance and support
body: Avoiding feared situations can restrict everyday life, and continual avoidance can worsen the problem. That is a general point about phobias from the NHS trust source.
Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) can help with phobias, and gradual exposure may be used with professional support. The sources point to seeking help if symptoms affect daily life.

2026-11-14-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Pediophobia is a descriptive name for fear of dolls. Humanlike doll faces can feel uncanny or unnerving, a subjective reaction that is not evidence a doll is alive or dangerous.
glance: Humanlike doll faces, experienced as uncanny or unnerving
On contact, or when thinking about the feared object
Can include palpitations, trembling, dizziness and chest tightness
CBT; gradual exposure or desensitization, with specialist support

sections.heading: The name and the uncanny face
body: Pediophobia is an established descriptive name meaning fear of dolls. Humanlike doll faces can be experienced as uncanny or unnerving. That is a subjective reaction. It is not evidence that a doll is alive or dangerous.

sections.heading: Contact, anticipation and avoidance
body: A phobia may cause anxiety or panic on contact with the feared object, or even when thinking about it, which is called anticipatory anxiety. Body alarm can include palpitations, trembling, dizziness and chest tightness.
Avoiding contact with the feared object is characteristic of phobias. Avoidance can come to organize daily life and to limit it.

sections.heading: Treatment with specialist support
body: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a treatment for phobias. Gradual exposure or desensitization can be part of treatment, with specialist support. The NHS sources point to professional help if fear affects daily life.

2026-11-14-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Scopophobia is a term for the fear of being watched or stared at, particularly by unfamiliar people. Fear of scrutiny can occur in social anxiety, and the name alone is not a diagnosis.
glance: Fear of being watched or stared at, particularly by unfamiliar people
Social anxiety, in which fear of scrutiny and negative judgment can occur
Sweating, trembling and rapid heart rate
No treatment trial specific to scopophobia is claimed

sections.heading: A name, not a diagnosis
body: Scopophobia is a term for fear of being watched or stared at, particularly by unfamiliar people. Fear of scrutiny and of negative judgment can occur in social anxiety. The descriptive name alone is not a diagnosis.

sections.heading: Feeling scrutinized
body: Anxiety can arise before a social situation. Possible bodily symptoms include sweating, trembling and a rapid heart rate.

Anxiety can occur even when there is no current threat. Feeling scrutinized does not establish actual danger, and it does not establish that other people have hostile intentions. Avoidance may feel helpful in the short term, while the anxiety remains without treatment.

sections.heading: What the treatment evidence covers
body: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is supported by research for social anxiety. Exposure therapy, which progressively confronts feared situations, is part of treatment. This evidence is about social anxiety in general. No treatment trial specific to scopophobia is claimed.
The sources point to professional help when anxiety interferes with everyday life. Treatment is tailored with a qualified clinician.

2026-11-17-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: A geyser is a hot spring with restricted underground plumbing. Water heated under pressure begins to boil, the pressure drops, more water boils, and expanding steam drives water and vapor out of the vent.
glance: A hot spring whose restricted underground plumbing limits free circulation
Can be built by silica deposited from thermal water

sections.heading: Water heated under pressure
body: Geysers are hot springs whose restricted underground plumbing limits free circulation. Surface water seeps underground and is heated by the volcanic geothermal system. Pressure increases with depth, and water under pressure can remain liquid above the temperature at which it boils at the surface.
In many studied geysers, bends or side chambers in the plumbing trap steam. Bubbles released from them heat the column of water above.

sections.heading: How an eruption starts and stops
body: The first boiling and overflow reduce the pressure. That allows more hot water to boil and the steam to expand. The expanding steam drives liquid water and vapor out of the vent. The visible white plume is largely condensed water droplets, not pure water vapor.
An eruption ends as the reservoir is depleted or the water cools. Replenishment and heating then permit another cycle.

sections.heading: Varied plumbing and silica cones
body: The underground shapes of geysers vary. The side-chamber cutaway in the infographic is a schematic, not a surveyed map of a particular geyser. Silica deposited from thermal water can build a cone around a geyser vent.

2026-11-17-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The southern mole cricket is a brown burrowing insect, native to South America and introduced to the southeastern United States. It digs with enlarged forelegs, and males call from a horn-shaped burrow opening that projects the sound skyward.
glance: Moist sandy or mucky open areas

sections.heading: A body built for digging
body: The southern mole cricket is Neoscapteriscus borellii, formerly Scapteriscus borellii. Adults are brown, with enlarged digging forelegs, forewings longer than the pronotum and hindwings that extend beyond the abdomen. Body length is 25 to 32 mm.

Neoscapteriscus has two blade-like dactyls on the tibia of each foreleg. In N. borellii they are separated at the base by at least half the basal width of a dactyl. Mole crickets force loose soil aside with strokes of the enlarged forelegs, and they spend nearly all their lives underground.

sections.heading: The calling burrow
body: Males call with a low, ringing trill from a horn-shaped burrow opening. These specialized calling burrows augment the sound and project it skyward, which attracts flying members of the same species, including females.
A generalized Neoscapteriscus calling burrow contains an opening horn, constrictions, a bulb, a turn-around, and surface and deep tunnels.

sections.heading: Where it lives and what it eats
body: The species is native to South America and has been introduced to the southeastern United States. Its habitat includes moist sandy or mucky open areas such as lawns, fields and the margins of ponds or streams. Southern mole crickets are omnivorous but largely carnivorous, and they mostly eat other insects.

sections.heading: Eggs, nymphs and generations
body: The eggs are gray-brown and bean-shaped, and they are laid in underground chambers. Nymphs resemble smaller, wingless adults. One generation a year is typical, except in south Florida, where there can be two. Eggs are laid in spring, and large nymphs or adults overwinter.

sections.heading: The generalized nervous system
body: The infographic's nervous-system view is a generalized insect schematic, not a measured dissection of this species. In that general plan, a brain on the upper (dorsal) side connects to a nerve cord on the lower (ventral) side, which has ganglia arranged by segment. The ganglia of the thorax supply nerves to the legs and wings.

2026-11-17-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Pillow lava forms when basalt enters water. The water chills the outside of the lava into a glassy rind, and the lava grows by budding one bulbous lobe after another.
glance: A glassy rind, chilled rapidly by water
A setting that was formerly underwater

sections.heading: How a pillow buds
body: Basalt entering water can form bulbous lobes called pillows. The water rapidly chills the outside of the lava into a glassy rind. A continued supply of lava expands the lobe until its rind cracks, and a new lobe buds out.

sections.heading: How pillows pile up and cool
body: Pillows accumulate in mounds, and they settle into the gaps between earlier pillows. As the interior of a pillow cools, joints can radiate inward from its surface.

sections.heading: A sign of former water
body: Ancient pillow basalts can indicate that the setting where they formed was once underwater, because these lobes take shape when basalt enters water.

2026-11-17-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The Hercules beetle is a scarab beetle whose range includes southern Mexico to Bolivia and the Lesser Antilles. Males carry horns on the head and thorax and use them to squeeze and lift rivals. Females have no horns.

sections.heading: Horns for squeezing and lifting
body: Dynastes hercules is a scarab beetle. Males bear horns on the head and on the thorax, and females lack horns. Males use the horns to squeeze and lift rivals in contests for access to females. The wing covers of males can be olive with dark spots, and females are usually black.

sections.heading: Life in decaying wood
body: The species undergoes complete metamorphosis, passing through egg, larva, pupa and adult. Larvae feed on dead wood in decaying logs. Adults generally feed on fallen, rotting fruit. The range includes southern Mexico to Bolivia and the Lesser Antilles, and it includes rainforest.

sections.heading: The generalized internal view
body: The internal section in the infographic is a generalized insect section, not one specific to the Hercules beetle. It includes a heart, gut, nerve cord, spiracle and trachea.

2026-11-17-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Cherenkov radiation is light produced when an electrically charged particle travels through a transparent medium, such as water, faster than light travels in that medium. It can produce the blue or violet glow in the water around a nuclear reactor core.
glance: Light from a charged particle that outruns light in a transparent medium
A blue or violet glow in water around a nuclear reactor core
The speed of light in vacuum
A sonic boom or a boat bow wave

sections.heading: Faster than light in water
body: Cherenkov radiation occurs when an electrically charged particle travels faster than light travels in the transparent medium around it. Light travels more slowly in water than in vacuum. That does not allow a particle to exceed the speed of light in vacuum. High-energy electrons are one example of charged particles that can produce Cherenkov radiation.

sections.heading: How the glow is made
body: The moving charged particle interacts with the medium, and the electromagnetic waves that are emitted reinforce into a shock wave of light. This emission can produce the blue or violet glow seen in the water around a nuclear reactor core.
The process can be compared with a sonic boom or with the bow wave of a boat. These are analogies, not identical phenomena. The diagrams in the infographic are conceptual and not to scale.

sections.heading: What it is used for
body: Cherenkov light is used in nuclear-material accounting. It is also used in particle physics to measure the energy and trajectory of particles.

2026-11-18-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The yellow tang is a lemon-yellow reef fish of the subtropical Pacific. It grazes algae from rocks by day, rests in crevices at night and carries a defensive spine on each side of its tail base.

Algae grazed from rocks and reef framework
A white spine on each side of the tail base

sections.heading: How to recognize it
body: The yellow tang has an oval, lemon-yellow body that is flattened from side to side, with large dorsal and anal fins and a small, downturned mouth. A white defensive spine sits on each side of the base of the tail. Adults grow to about 15 to 20 cm, or 6 to 8 inches.

sections.heading: Where it lives
body: Its native range is the subtropical Pacific, including Hawaii and western Pacific islands toward Japan. It lives on reefs, at depths that include 2 to 46 m. Individuals may occur alone or in loose groups, and juveniles can be territorial.

sections.heading: Grazing by day, resting at night
body: The yellow tang grazes algae from rocks and the reef framework with flexible, comb-like teeth and its small downturned mouth. This grazing helps limit the competition between algae and coral.
Grazing is a daytime activity. At night the fish rests alone in reef crevices, and its color is grayish-yellow with a white band along the side.

sections.heading: The blades at the tail base
body: The blades at the base of the tail are modified scales that sit in slots. Flexing the tail exposes them. The fish uses them in defense and in competition. They can inflict deep wounds, so touching the fish is to be avoided.

sections.heading: What this means for an aquarium
body: The aquarium notes on the infographic are qualitative inferences from the biology, not numeric husbandry prescriptions. They point to algae-based feeding and reef-like refuges for the night. Because of territorial behavior, grouping in the wild is not a guarantee of peaceful tankmates. Grazing around coral is not, on its own, a guarantee that the fish is compatible with every reef tank.

2026-11-18-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The copperband butterflyfish, also called the beaked coralfish, is a silvery-white fish with orange-copper bars. The adult uses its long snout to extract bottom-living invertebrates from holes and crevices.

sections.heading: How to recognize it
body: The body is silvery-white with three broad orange-copper bars. A narrower orange bar with dark margins runs through the eye. The dorsal and anal fins are tall, and the dorsal fin carries an eyespot. A dark bar with blue edging crosses the base of the tail. The maximum length is 20 cm, or 8 inches.
Chelmon rostratus is the accepted species name. Copperband butterflyfish and beaked coralfish are both common names for this fish.

sections.heading: Where it lives
body: The copperband butterflyfish has a tropical Indo-West Pacific range. It lives along rocky shores, on coral reefs, in estuaries and on silty inner reefs, at a preferred depth of 1 to 25 m. It is encountered singly or in pairs, and it forms pairs during breeding.

sections.heading: A snout for holes and crevices
body: The adult's long snout extracts bottom-living invertebrates from holes and crevices. The long snout develops after the larva has settled.

sections.heading: In an aquarium
body: The Georgia Aquarium describes this fish as difficult to keep in home aquariums. It is sometimes used to control Aiptasia.

Its diet of bottom-living invertebrates and its occasional use against Aiptasia do not establish that it is safe for every reef tank. Compatibility and feeding need to be assessed, and pest control cannot be promised. This is a cautious husbandry implication of the documented diet, not a claim that all individuals eat the same ornamental animals.

2026-11-18-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The flame angelfish is an orange-red fish with black vertical bars from western and central Pacific reefs. It is secretive, stays close to shelter and feeds mainly on bottom algae and detritus.

Rich lagoon and seaward coral reefs at 5 to 60 m

sections.heading: How to recognize it
body: Typical flame angelfish have orange-red bodies with an orange-yellow midbody, black vertical bars and a dark blotch behind the pectoral fin. Blue and purple streaks highlight the rear of the dorsal and anal fins. The tail fin has light orange-yellow rays with translucent membranes, and the pelvic fins are orange-red.

sections.heading: Where it lives
body: The species occurs across scattered reef localities in the western and central Pacific, including Palau, the Marshall Islands and the Society Islands. Its habitat is rich lagoon and seaward coral reefs at 5 to 60 m. It is a secretive fish that stays close to shelter. Its primary foods in the wild are algae growing on the bottom and detritus.

sections.heading: Harems and sex change
body: Flame angelfish are protogynous, which means females can change into males. Wild males maintain harems, and spawning typically occurs at dusk.

sections.heading: Guidance from an aquaculture producer
body: The husbandry guidance comes from Biota, an aquaculture producer. Biota describes a typical captive size of about 4 inches (approximately 10 cm), which is not a species maximum. It recommends an aquarium of at least 65 US gallons (approximately 246 liters) for adults. That is a producer guideline, not a universal threshold.
Biota recommends varied, nutritious food and frequent feeding. The fish also pick at rockwork for algae and sponges. They are territorial with their own species and with other dwarf angels.
Biota rates the fish reef safe with caution. Individuals may pick at soft corals, clams and fleshy large-polyp stony corals, and feeding does not establish guaranteed coral safety.

sections.heading: Planning a tank, and never releasing
body: Shelter-rich rockwork and algae-based food reflect the shelter association and grazing biology of the species in the wild. Aquarium space and compatibility need individual planning. Aquarium fish should never be released. The U.S. Geological Survey identifies probable aquarium release among the pathways by which this species has been introduced.

2026-11-18-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The pajama cardinalfish is a small western Pacific fish that hides among branching corals by day and leaves them at night to feed on small crustaceans. The male incubates the eggs in his mouth.

Small shrimps, crabs and other small crustaceans

sections.heading: How to recognize it
body: The pajama cardinalfish, also called the coral cardinalfish, has a yellow head, large red eyes and two dorsal fins. A vertical black bar runs beneath the first dorsal fin, and large brown spots mark the rear of the body. The maximum reported length is 8.5 cm, about 3.3 inches.

sections.heading: Life among branching corals
body: This fish lives in the western Pacific, in lagoons, bays and sheltered coastal coral reefs. The Oregon Coast Aquarium records depths to 14 m. It lives among branching corals, including Porites cylindrica, Acropora and Anacropora.
It forms social groups. The fish hide by day and leave the protection of the coral to feed at night. The species is a carnivore that feeds on small shrimps, crabs and other small crustaceans.

sections.heading: Eggs carried in the mouth
body: The male incubates the fertilized eggs in his mouth and does not feed during incubation. No precise length of incubation is given.

sections.heading: In an aquarium
body: The aquarium guidance comes mainly from a care guide by Coralife, a manufacturer. The fish is described as generally peaceful toward other tankmates and as reef safe. That does not imply safety for every small crustacean, since crustaceans are its natural prey. Groups can develop dominance hierarchies and need a larger aquarium with ample cover.

The guide advises a varied meaty diet. Some fish refuse dry foods at first. They can be coaxed with frozen food and later weaned to dry, and feeding at night is worth trying for reluctant feeders. Coralife lists a minimum of 20 US gallons (approximately 76 liters). That is not presented as a universal recommendation for housing groups, which need more room and cover.

sections.heading: How to recognize it
body: The yellow watchman goby, also called the yellow shrimp goby and the banded prawn goby, is yellow with fine pale blue or white spots on the head and upper body. Faint brown bars can occur. The yellow phase and the whitish barred phase are the same species. The fish can reach about 10 cm, approximately 4 inches.

sections.heading: Where it lives
body: This is a marine goby of the eastern Indian Ocean and western Pacific. It lives on the sandy bottoms of seagrass beds, lagoons and sheltered coral reefs, at 2 to 15 m depth in the Oregon Coast Aquarium account.

sections.heading: A burrow shared with a shrimp
body: The goby shares its burrow with an alpheid shrimp. The shrimp builds and maintains the burrow. The goby guards it and warns of approaching predators, and the two communicate by touch and movement.

sections.heading: In an aquarium
body: The aquarium guidance comes from a care guide by Coralife, a manufacturer. It recommends varied meat-based foods and says this bottom-feeding fish can learn to feed in mid-water. The Oregon Coast Aquarium account lists algae and bivalves, so no universal claim about its diet is made.

Coralife describes the fish as generally peaceful and reef-safe, and advises against keeping it with others of its own species, except as mated pairs. Reef compatibility is guidance, not a guarantee for every individual or community.

The guide calls for sand or fine gravel deep enough for burrowing, rocks secured on the tank bottom so they cannot settle onto the fish, and a secure lid, because the fish can jump. The manufacturer's minimum is 30 US gallons, approximately 114 liters. That is a minimum recommendation, not a guarantee for any stocking plan.

2026-11-18-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The orchid dottyback is a small purple fish known only from the Red Sea. It darts from reef ledges to feed on passing zooplankton and returns to shelter, and the male tends the eggs in a nook or cave.

sections.heading: How to recognize it
body: The orchid dottyback is a purple to magenta fish. A black line through the eye is its diagnostic mark. Under aquarium lighting the fish shows purple. In the wild, the filtering of red light can make fish in deeper water appear blue. The recorded maximum total length is 6.3 cm, about 2.5 inches.

sections.heading: Life on Red Sea rock faces
body: The species is known only from the Red Sea. It is a marine, reef-associated fish that lives on vertical rock faces or beneath overhangs and takes refuge in small holes. It darts out from reef ledges to feed on passing zooplankton, then returns to shelter.

sections.heading: Eggs in nooks and caves
body: The eggs form a mass held by filamentous threads. The mass is deposited in nooks or caves and tended by the male.
Captive breeding is established. One published study of captive fish found an incubation of approximately 96 hours at 27 ± 1 degrees Celsius. That is the result of one study, not a universal timer.

sections.heading: In an aquarium
body: The aquarium guidance comes from the culture and care notes of ORA, Biota and Proaquatix. Foods for cultured fish include mysid and brine shrimp, krill, pellets and flakes. The fish is moderately territorial and should have many hiding places. It may fight others of its own species and similar-looking fish. Being more peaceful than many other dottybacks does not mean it is free of aggression.

It is generally compatible with corals but may chase very small shrimp, so reef-safe is not a guarantee for every small mobile invertebrate. Biota suggests a tank size of 30 US gallons, approximately 114 liters. That is husbandry guidance, not a biological threshold from the wild.

2026-11-19-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Ménière disease is an inner-ear condition whose symptoms come and go: spinning vertigo, hearing loss, tinnitus and ear fullness. Its underlying cause remains unclear, and there is no cure yet.
glance: Spinning vertigo, hearing loss, tinnitus, ear fullness, sometimes nausea or vomiting

sections.heading: Inside the inner ear
body: The labyrinth of the inner ear contains the cochlea, for hearing, and the semicircular canals and otolith organs, including the utricle and saccule, for balance. The membranous labyrinth contains endolymph.
A buildup of endolymph, called endolymphatic hydrops, is associated with disrupted hearing and balance signals in Ménière disease. Its underlying cause remains unclear.

sections.heading: Episodes of symptoms
body: Symptoms come and go. They are spinning vertigo, hearing loss, tinnitus, ear fullness, and sometimes nausea or vomiting. Usually one ear is affected.

sections.heading: Diagnosis and management
body: Diagnosis uses the history of symptoms and hearing testing, with evaluation for other causes. There is no single definitive test.

There is no cure yet. Medicines directed by a clinician may help the symptoms of an attack, hearing aids may help hearing loss, and vestibular rehabilitation may help persistent balance problems. Reducing salt in the diet is something to discuss with a clinician. It may help some people, but it is not a cure.

sections.heading: Driving and stroke warning signs
body: The NHS guidance is not to drive during dizziness or when vertigo is coming on. Vertigo with new facial droop, arm weakness or speech difficulty may be a stroke, and the guidance is to call emergency services immediately.

2026-11-19-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) commonly involves plaque building up in arteries, narrowing them and reducing blood flow to the legs and feet. It can cause leg pain with walking, and some people have no symptoms.
glance: Leg muscle pain with walking that eases after a few minutes of rest
Ankle-brachial index, comparing blood pressure at the ankle and arm
Higher heart attack and stroke risk

sections.heading: Narrowed arteries in the leg
body: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. PAD commonly involves a buildup of plaque that narrows arteries and reduces blood flow to the legs and feet. The infographic shows a schematic of the arterial supply of the leg, with a magnified view of an artery narrowed by plaque and reduced flow beyond it. It does not present a vein or a clot as the usual cause. PAD is associated with a higher risk of heart attack and stroke.

sections.heading: Pain with walking
body: Intermittent claudication is leg muscle pain with walking that eases after a few minutes of rest. The calves are commonly affected. Some people have no symptoms. Other symptoms can include cold feet, weakness or numbness, and sores that do not heal.

sections.heading: Evaluation and management
body: Evaluation includes clinical assessment and an ankle-brachial index, which compares blood pressure at the ankle and the arm.

Management may include an exercise program guided by a clinician, stopping smoking, prescribed medicines and, in selected cases, procedures to improve blood flow. The guidance also covers controlling blood pressure and cholesterol and, for people with diabetes, managing blood sugar and looking after the feet.

sections.heading: Acute limb ischemia
body: Acute limb ischemia is an emergency. A foot that is paler or colder than the other, being unable to feel or move the foot, or pain or pins and needles at rest requires immediate medical help. The guidance is to call 911.

2026-11-19-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: An inguinal hernia is a bulge of abdominal contents, often fat or small intestine, through a weak area of the lower abdominal wall at the groin. Most patients need surgical repair, and strangulation requires emergency care.
glance: Abdominal contents bulging through a weak area of the lower abdominal wall
Strangulation, when blood supply is cut off

sections.heading: A passage through the abdominal wall
body: An inguinal hernia is abdominal contents bulging through a weak area of the lower abdominal wall at the groin. The contents often include fat or small intestine. The peritoneum forms a sac around the hernia. The inguinal canals are passages through the lower abdominal wall.

Indirect hernias relate to an opening present at birth. Direct hernias relate to weakness of the wall that develops later. Family history and aging are associated with increased risk. Chronic cough, constipation and repeated heavy lifting may contribute through increased abdominal pressure.

sections.heading: Symptoms and diagnosis
body: A groin bulge, aching, burning or heaviness may worsen with coughing, straining, lifting or prolonged standing and improve when lying down. Clinical history and examination are used for diagnosis. Imaging may help when the diagnosis is unclear.

sections.heading: Repair or watchful waiting
body: Most patients need surgical repair. Open or laparoscopic repair may use mesh to reinforce the weak area. Watchful waiting, with regular medical follow-up, may be appropriate for some men with few or no symptoms. That is not advice for everyone.

sections.heading: Trapped and strangulated hernias
body: Incarceration means the contents are trapped. Strangulation means the blood supply is cut off, and it requires emergency care. Sudden severe pain, a bulge that is suddenly larger or newly irreducible, fever, redness, nausea or vomiting are reasons to seek urgent medical help. Obstruction may cause bloating.

2026-11-20-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Cats need protection from things they perceive as dangers, including unfamiliar environments. A secure retreat helps a cat feel protected, and how a cat responds to an unfamiliar object varies from one cat to another.
glance: Protection from perceived dangers, including unfamiliar environments
May be a cardboard box or carrier the cat can enter and leave
Individual cats differ; fearful cats may react more strongly

sections.heading: Why a retreat matters
body: Cats need protection from perceived dangers, and unfamiliar environments are among them. A secure retreat helps a cat feel protected.
A safe place may be a cardboard box or a carrier. It has sides that surround the cat, and the cat is able to enter and leave. Raised safe places are often preferred.

sections.heading: Smells, sounds and sudden objects
body: Cats use smell to evaluate their surroundings. Unfamiliar smells or sounds can be stressful. The sudden appearance of a novel object may provoke a startle response. Individual cats differ, and fearful cats may react more strongly.
The Cornell source says not to startle cats deliberately with surprise objects. A frightened cat can associate the event with the place where it happened or with the person involved.

sections.heading: What the picture does and does not show
body: The infographic illustrates a cat that may observe, approach and retreat. These are possible responses. They are not a sequence that every cat must follow, and they are not a diagnosis. Individual responses vary.

2026-11-20-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: Arginine is an essential amino acid that cats must get from their diet. It takes part in detoxifying ammonia, which is released when protein is broken down.
glance: The urea cycle, which converts ammonia to urea
Cats make only limited arginine in their own bodies
Can cause ammonia accumulation, vomiting, neurological signs and potentially death

sections.heading: What arginine is
body: Arginine is an essential amino acid and a building block of proteins. Cats require it in their diet. They can make only limited amounts of arginine in their own bodies, so they depend on the supply from food.

sections.heading: The ammonia link
body: The breakdown of protein releases ammonia, and arginine takes part in detoxifying it. The urea cycle converts ammonia to urea, with arginine as an important intermediate. The infographic explains this with a simplified metabolic schematic.

sections.heading: Deficiency and diet
body: Arginine deficiency can cause ammonia to accumulate, with vomiting, neurological signs and potentially death. A carefully formulated, complete feline diet accounts for these special nutrient requirements. An all-meat diet is not balanced.

2026-11-20-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The darker face, ears, legs and tail of a Siamese cat follow skin temperature. Pigment is produced more readily in cooler skin and inefficiently at the warmer skin temperatures of the trunk.
glance: Darker face, ears, legs and tail in a seal-point Siamese
Variants of the tyrosinase gene TYR
Replacement fur can grow back darker

sections.heading: Pigment that depends on temperature
body: Siamese pigmentation is associated with variants of the tyrosinase gene, TYR. In Siamese cats, pigment production is inefficient at the warmer skin temperatures of the trunk. It occurs more readily in cooler skin.

sections.heading: Why the points are dark
body: In a seal-point Siamese, the face, ears, legs and tail are normally cooler than the central body, and they are darker. These darker areas are the points of the coat pattern.

sections.heading: Fur that grows back darker
body: When body fur is lost in cold conditions, the exposed skin is cooler. As the fur grows back, that cooler skin can produce darker replacement fur.

2026-11-20-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: A bottom-hung window that tilts inward creates a narrowing gap at its side. A cat can become trapped there, and the compression of blood vessels and nerves is potentially life-threatening.
glance: A narrowing gap at the side
Between the last rib and pelvis, or by a hindlimb
Potentially life-threatening; requires urgent veterinary attention

sections.heading: How a cat gets trapped
body: Bottom-hung windows tilt inward and create a narrowing gap at the side, in which cats can become trapped. A cat's attempts to escape can cause it to slide downward in the gap. The cat may be caught between the last rib and the pelvis, or the entrapment may involve a hindlimb.

sections.heading: What the compression does
body: Compression of blood vessels reduces blood flow to the muscles, nerves and spinal cord. Direct compression of nerves also contributes to the injury. Neurological injury may cause weakness or paralysis of the hindlimbs.

sections.heading: When blood flow returns
body: The restoration of blood flow can cause reperfusion injury, with further tissue damage and serious complications that affect the whole body. Window entrapment is potentially life-threatening and requires urgent veterinary attention.

2026-11-20-factual-infographic-factual-i.dek: The third eyelid, or nictitating membrane, is a whitish-pink membrane at the inner corner of a cat's eye. It extends across the eye to help protect it from scratches, and its glands contribute to the watery part of tears.
